projects.title: Automated image analysis of tau fibrils in the human Alzheimer's disease brain
projects.summary: The project aims to detect tau fibrils within tau tangles in human Alzheimer's disease brain tissue, imaged with correlative light and electron microscopy, and measure their twist to study tangle stages. The student would develop a Python image analysis workflow for denoising, line detection, segmentation and machine learning-based pixel classification.

projects.title: Analysis of dendritic spine changes using deep-learning encoding in a latent space
projects.summary: The project aims to develop a deep-learning system that reconstructs the temporal evolution of dendritic spine shapes. Spine shapes from time-lapse 3D microscopy would be encoded into a low-dimensional latent space to classify single-spine behaviours and study neural plasticity.

projects.title: From PDE to Cell Imaging: A Multiresolution Framework for Fourier Ptychography
projects.summary: Build a PDE/wavelets-inspired multiresolution reconstruction algorithm for Fourier ptychographic microscopy, representing the high-resolution complex image with box-spline basis functions and refining from low to high frequencies to avoid poor local minima in the non-convex loss. The student will combine an existing Python Fourier ptychography library with a box-spline modelling library.

projects.title: Multigrid Solver For Non-Uniform Sampling With TV Regularization
projects.summary: Develop a fast solver for the non-uniform interpolation problem based on the multigrid scheme. The underlying image is represented with box-splines, with a focus on TV-based regularizers, implemented in PyTorch.

projects.title: Penalized Maximum Likelihood Approach for Deconvolution of Microscopy with Learned Convex Regularizer
projects.summary: The project addresses deconvolution of microscopy images, where measurements are a convolution of the ground truth with a known blur kernel and are corrupted by Poisson noise. The student will derive a variational formulation of the problem, solve it with a suitable optimization approach, and benchmark a state-of-the-art learned convex data-driven regularizer.

projects.title: Prediction and survival analysis of ovarian cancer through multimodal fusion of radiomic and multiomic data.
projects.summary: A six-month master's project on personalized treatment of high-grade serous ovarian cancer. It aims to fuse radiomics features from CT/MRI with multiomics data to build predictive and survival models, with attention to feature robustness and reproducibility. The work is part of the ERC-funded MROMICS initiative and is based at the Montpellier Cancer Institute (PINKCC lab).

projects.title: Sparse Unrolled Auto-Encoders for Interpretable Analysis of Neural Data
projects.summary: The project investigates sparse autoencoder-style interpretable deep learning for understanding neural computation. It builds on the DUNL (Deconvolutional Unrolled Learning) framework, which unrolls ISTA for convolutional sparse coding, and explores unrolling the greedy Matching Pursuit algorithm as a simpler-to-tune and easier-to-explain alternative.

projects.title: Diffusion Models for Magnetic Resonance Imaging Reconstruction
projects.summary: Develop and evaluate diffusion-model priors for reconstructing MRI images from undersampled k-space data. The work compares baseline 2D diffusion reconstructions with the lab's in-house deep learning method, explores new architectures and reconstruction frameworks, and assesses the feasibility of 3D diffusion reconstruction for MRI.

projects.title: Inverse Problems with ℓ1 Regularization: Extreme Points of the Regularization Polytope and Analysis vs Synthesis Formulations
projects.summary: Determine the extreme points of the regularization polytope {x : ||Lx||₁ ≤ 1} defined by a regularization operator L, in order to analyze solution structure and enable a synthesis formulation of ℓ1-regularized inverse problems. The student studies background on inverse problems and sparsity, then designs and implements an algorithm to compute these extreme points for a given L.

projects.title: Discretization of Non-Uniform Sampling Problems with Exponential Splines
projects.summary: Recover a continuous-time signal from noisy non-uniform samples by solving an inverse problem with generalized total-variation (gTV) regularization. The student studies L-spline theory and exponential splines, discretizes the problem with B-splines, and solves the resulting finite-dimensional optimisation problem with suitable algorithms.

projects.title: Likelihoods for Hawkes Processes
projects.summary: The student will study a recently proposed binned likelihood for estimating the excitation kernel of Hawkes processes, which is easier to optimise than the classical likelihood when many events are observed or the process is near or above criticality. Tasks include simulating Hawkes process trajectories, implementing estimators based on the classical and binned likelihoods, and comparing their strengths and weaknesses.

projects.title: Sampling from Learned Regularizers
projects.summary: The project studies posterior sampling for linear inverse problems using energy-based models built from learnable potential functions applied to linear filter responses. The goal is to implement and analyze sampling algorithms such as the (annealed) Metropolis adjusted Langevin algorithm for uncertainty quantification.

projects.title: Improving Optimization Algorithms for Ptychography Phase Retrieval
projects.summary: Explore and improve the convergence and efficiency of optimization algorithms for ptychography phase retrieval. The student will implement and compare strategies such as quasi-Newton and conjugate gradient, with explicit or automatic-differentiation gradients, and possibly investigate GPU acceleration schedules and adaptive hyperparameter selection.

projects.title: High-Dimensional Gaussian Sampling: Cholesky versus Markov
projects.summary: Compares three approaches to generating high-dimensional Gaussian samples: exact Cholesky-factorization linear algebra, iterative Markov Chain Monte Carlo, and Perturb-and-Map. The goal is to find the best trade-off between computational speed and statistical accuracy for large-scale inverse problems.

projects.title: Vector-Valued Inverse Problems: B-Spline Discretization and Identification of Matrix Differential Operators for Regularization
projects.summary: Design and implement a Python package for two-dimensional vector spline functions based on matrices of differential operators (MDOs), and validate it on a synthetic or real-world problem. The project also studies vector-valued inverse problems regularized with an MDO, aiming to identify or learn a suitable MDO from observations of correlated vector-valued signals.

projects.title: Exploring Global Youth Art Through AI: A Semantic Analysis of the IMAJ Collection
projects.summary: Semantic analysis of a database of more than 100,000 drawings by young artists aged 3 to 25 from 150 countries, collected by IMAJ. The project will evaluate large language models on curated subsets before scaling up to generate textual interpretations and enrich the metadata of the collection.

projects.title: Investigating steerable wavelets to build Parseval frames
projects.summary: Develop a learned, convex regularizer for image reconstruction based on a parametric, steerable wavelet framework that controls filter scale and orientation with a compact parameter set. The regularizer is trained via denoising and validated on diverse inverse problems using accelerated gradient methods.

projects.title: Training Complex-Valued Denoisers for Phase Retrieval
projects.summary: The project aims to train a denoiser that operates directly on complex-valued data, regularizing magnitude and phase jointly for phase retrieval. The student will study amplitude-phase coupling across imaging modalities, build complex-valued datasets, and compare Plug-and-Play, diffusion and flow-matching paradigms against magnitude/phase splitting.

projects.title: Continuous-Domain Phase Retrieval in Dimension One
projects.summary: Develop and benchmark a coarse-to-fine (multiscale) numerical solver for recovering a complex-valued continuous-domain signal from magnitude-only linear measurements. The solver starts with Wirtinger Flow at a coarse scale and propagates estimates up the resolution hierarchy, and is compared with single-scale Wirtinger Flow with spectral initialization at full resolution.

projects.title: 789 – Spine motion replication
projects.summary: Replicate the spine motion of quadruped locomotion with fewer actuators than a fully articulated spine would need, reducing weight and mechanical complexity. The project is 100% software.

projects.title: 784 – Modeling zebrafish sensorimotor integration using simulation and robots
projects.summary: Model zebrafish sensorimotor integration using neuromechanical simulation and the ZBot fish-like robot, in an ongoing collaboration with Duke University. Possible avenues include improving the FARMS simulation framework, applying deep reinforcement learning to sensory-motor circuits, and studying visually-guided behaviors.

projects.title: 734 – Firmware development for ENVIROBOT
projects.summary: Continue the development of ENVIROBOT by adapting the existing firmware to a new electronic board and extending it with new functionality. The work is mainly software on an embedded microcontroller platform.

projects.title: 783 – Paleorobotics of Armored Tail Strikes: Simulation, Compliance, and Energy Dissipation in Extinct Mammalian Weapons
projects.summary: Use paleorobotics to test whether extinct armored mammals could generate powerful tail-club strikes, by building MuJoCo and SIMM/OpenSim-type models of a tendon-driven tail and mapping strike energy dissipation. Optional work includes a biomimetic carapace and a tendon-driven tail prototype, split between EPFL and University of Zurich.

projects.title: 782 – Radio communication module on 169.4 MHz
projects.summary: Finalize a prototype bidirectional serial link based on a CC1120 radio chip at 169.4 MHz, by redesigning the PCBs, improving communication software and stability, adding a simple user interface on the microcontroller, and adding flow control on the robot side.

projects.title: 729 – Robotic paleontology: tail strike defense
projects.summary: Design, build and control a life-sized robotic tail to replicate a dinosaur's club-tail strike, and measure impact force and velocity using fossil-based bone-like material at Empa Dübendorf. The thesis combines mechanical design, microcontroller programming, force measurements and data analysis.

projects.title: 786 – (New!) User-Centric Multimodal Interaction for Assistive Robotic Environments
projects.summary: Study the everyday challenges of wheelchair users and investigate how multiple user interfaces (markerless body-language tracking, LLM/VLM natural-language control, tablet) can give accessible control of mobile robotic furniture. The student can further develop or evaluate one interaction modality.

projects.title: 785 – (New!) Mobile Manipulation of Assistive Robotic Furniture
projects.summary: Integrate a robot arm with a mobile robotic furniture platform and develop a whole-body controller so that a mobile table can fetch objects for a wheelchair user, e.g. bringing a cup of water. The goal is an end-to-end demonstration in MuJoCo simulation and in the real world.

projects.title: Project 1: Comparing Representational Hierarchies in Neural Networks
projects.summary: Investigates how layer selection and aggregation shape conclusions about representational similarity between neural networks. The goal is a principled way to compare models across their full representational hierarchies, distinguishing isolated layer matches from agreement across the hierarchy, and reassessing evidence for representational convergence.

projects.title: Project 2: What Do Language Models Need from 3D Encoders?
projects.summary: Studies what 3D encoders (point clouds or Gaussian splats) contribute when connected to a language model for 3D scene reasoning, and how 3D representations could be learned to be more useful to LLMs. Starts from existing 3D encoders and a controlled 3D LLM pipeline, and extends to modeling spatial organization of cells.

projects.title: Project 3: Learning patient-level predictions from the spatial proteome
projects.summary: Develops a multiple instance learning approach for patient-level prediction from spatial single-cell proteomics data, aggregating information across spatial scales from single cells to niches and whole-tissue organization. Evaluation on public multiplexed imaging cohorts with patient-level outcomes such as cancer survival, including data efficiency and agreement of attended regions with known pathology.

projects.title: Project 4: Improving agents for single-cell genomics and biomedical discovery
projects.summary: Aims to improve the reasoning capabilities of LLM-based agents for single-cell biology tasks using agentic reinforcement learning, so that the agents can plan, execute computational workflows, and formulate hypotheses for biomedical discovery.

projects.summary: Proposes using graph neural networks to learn coarser graph embeddings of fine-scale landscape features, so that resistance distance-based gene flow predictions become computationally tractable at higher spatial resolution. Directions include graph coarsening strategies, approximation error bounds, and validation on synthetic and real ecological data.

projects.summary: Develop an algebraic multigrid (AMG) solver in JAX that supports automatic differentiation and GPU acceleration, for scientific machine learning workflows requiring differentiable iterative linear solves. The work involves analysing existing Python and Julia AMG implementations and designing a JAX-compatible architecture.

projects.title: Finding Slow Components in a Graph
projects.summary: The project studies how many random shortest-path distance queries are needed to identify a set of vertices V_1 whose incident edge weights are much larger than the rest of a weighted graph with exponentially distributed weights. It includes simulations on a range of graphs, evaluation of accuracy and sample complexity, and theoretical accuracy bounds.

projects.title: Reusable Foundations for Probabilistic Proofs in Lean
projects.summary: Develop a reusable Lean library on top of Mathlib providing foundations for probability (beyond existing martingales, concentration inequalities and CLT, e.g. Markov chains, random walks, couplings), so probabilists can formalize their results more easily. If time allows, the library would be used to formalize a paper on random graphs and branching processes.

projects.title: Reusable Foundations for Probabilistic Proofs in Lean
projects.summary: Build a coherent, reusable framework of formalized tools for probabilistic reasoning in Lean, extending existing martingale and central limit theorem support with missing pieces such as Markov chains and couplings. The aim is to make formalization more accessible to probabilists.

projects.title: Finding Slow Components in a Graph
projects.summary: Study an information spreading process on a graph in which some parts transmit information more slowly than others. The project asks how to recover the slow component from measured transmission speeds between vertices, and how recovery differs between random and adaptive measurement strategies.

projects.title: High-performance differentiable AMG in JAX with GPU acceleration
projects.summary: Develop a high-performance algebraic multigrid (AMG) linear solver in JAX that supports automatic differentiation and GPU acceleration. The goal is to enable efficient gradient-based optimization in scientific machine learning and differentiable physics applications requiring large linear system solves.

projects.title: Accelerating ecological connectivity analysis with graph neural networks
projects.summary: Develop a graph neural network approach that maps fine-scale landscape features onto lower-dimensional graph representations to speed up ecological connectivity analysis. The aim is high-resolution gene flow predictions across fragmented landscapes, with applications to conservation planning and identifying ecological corridors.

projects.title: Development and characterization of an acoustic matched source
projects.summary: The project aims to develop and characterize an acoustic matched source, using active control of a closed-box electrodynamic loudspeaker to achieve impedance matching. It includes a literature review, numerical FDTD/Simulink modelling, experimental measurements at multiple harmonics, and an extension to a broadband matched source using a corona discharge actuator.

projects.title: Enhancing Protein Design Through Advanced Graph Neural Networks
projects.summary: The project focuses on protein sequence design, creating protein sequences that perform specific functions for applications such as drug development and bioengineering. It will use advanced Graph Neural Networks to improve protein sequence design methods.

projects.title: Modeling translation elongation dynamics through Variational AutoEncoders
projects.summary: The project models ribosome profiling density profiles with Variational AutoEncoders to capture translation elongation dynamics. The student first evaluates VAE reconstruction in a single condition, then extends the decoder to take nutrient availability into account.

projects.title: Optimization of corona discharge loudspeakers
projects.summary: The project aims to identify and implement corona discharge loudspeaker configurations with better sound radiation efficiency, notably a useful band-pass behaviour over a wide audible band. It will build a COMSOL and/or analytical model of the transducer for geometry optimization, then build and test prototypes in anechoic conditions.

projects.title: Design of unprecedented sound sources: a dream come true with plasma loudspeakers?
projects.summary: The project aims to identify and, if possible, implement a purely omnidirectional corona discharge (plasma) loudspeaker configuration approximating an ideal pulsating sphere, and optionally extend the work to other canonical electroacoustic sources. The work involves COMSOL and/or analytical modelling for geometry optimisation, followed by prototype construction and anechoic testing.

projects.title: 3D Sound Localization
projects.summary: Build a toolbox that simulates human auditory localization to objectively assess how hearing aid algorithms preserve or distort spatial cues, replacing costly listening tests. The project has three stages: building a hearing-loss-aware 3D localization toolbox, measuring the HRTF of a Kemar dummy head, and validating the toolbox with listening tests involving about 10 normal-hearing and 20 hearing-impaired participants.

projects.title: Auditory distance perception
projects.summary: Evaluate how hearing aids affect the auditory distance perception of hearing-impaired listeners. The project has two stages: building a listening test facility with a loudspeaker on a precise motorised rail, then running listening tests with about 10 normal-hearing and 20 hearing-impaired participants.

projects.title: Exploration and improvement of a data-agnostic multimodal deep learning architecture relying on a novel fusion strategy
projects.summary: Explore, improve and propose alterations of a data-agnostic, perceiver-based multimodal deep learning architecture that integrates modalities sequentially. The work includes adapting layers for efficiency or performance, researching pre-training approaches, and evaluating data encoding tactics and hybrid fusion methods.

projects.title: Development of a Graphical User Interface for Electroacoustic Absorbers
projects.summary: The student reviews the literature on Electroacoustic Absorbers (EA), builds an analytical Matlab model, and implements direct impedance control on a prototype using a Speedgoat real-time target with Matlab/Simulink. The project ends with a stand-alone GUI that lets a non-expert set control parameters and assess an EA's acoustic performance in an impedance tube.

projects.title: Plasmacoustic headphones
projects.summary: Simulate and implement a fully open corona-discharge (CD) headphone, optimizing the transducer geometry with a COMSOL and/or analytical model, then building prototypes and testing them on an artificial ear in anechoic conditions. The goal is to avoid the occlusion effect of conventional headphones while managing sound leakage to the environment.

projects.title: Controlling the timbre of wind instruments with active control
projects.summary: Develop a scaled prototype of an active wind instrument: a cylindrical hollow duct with a ring of active electroacoustic absorbers that change the acoustic impedance and alter the timbre. The work covers COMSOL FEM simulations, design and control of the prototype, and acoustic assessment of the resonators and the whole instrument.

projects.title: VENOVA : an actively modified cylindrical cross-saxophone
projects.summary: The project aims to design an actuator and couplings (CAD and 3D printing) added to the VENOVA instrument, then model how impedance control at the actuator can alter its sound, and implement, measure and playtest control strategies. Some experience with reed instruments is preferable but not required.

projects.title: Controlling the timbre of wind instruments with active control
projects.summary: Studies wind instruments as axisymmetric hollow ducts with varying or constant cross-section, with the aim of controlling their timbre actively. The page excerpt is truncated.

projects.title: Plasmacoustic headphones
projects.summary: Explores headphones based on the corona discharge principle, which can produce a linear acoustic flow velocity source without a conventional membrane. The page excerpt is truncated.

projects.title: Development of a Graphical User Interface for Electroacoustic Absorbers
projects.summary: Aims to develop a graphical user interface for Electroacoustic Absorbers, which rely on a closed-box loudspeaker whose membrane is given a prescribed acoustic impedance. The page excerpt is truncated.

projects.title: Exploration and improvement of a data-agnostic multimodal deep learning architecture relying on a novel fusion strategy
projects.summary: Explores and improves a data-agnostic multimodal deep learning architecture based on a novel fusion strategy for learning from multiple information channels (modalities).

projects.title: Auditory distance perception
projects.summary: Studies auditory distance perception, which supports spatial awareness, object localization and obstacle avoidance. The page excerpt is truncated.

projects.title: 3D Sound Localization
projects.summary: Studies how sounds are localized in space, i.e. spatial hearing. The page excerpt is truncated.

projects.title: Design of unprecedented sound sources: a dream come true with plasma loudspeakers?
projects.summary: Investigates spherical sound sources, considered an optimal geometry due to limited scattering, using plasma loudspeakers. The page excerpt is truncated.

projects.title: Optimization of corona discharge loudspeakers
projects.summary: Aims to optimize corona discharge loudspeakers, which produce a linear acoustic flow velocity source without a conventional membrane. The page excerpt is truncated.

projects.title: Modeling translation elongation dynamics through Variational AutoEncoders
projects.summary: Models translation elongation dynamics from ribosome profiling data, which measures codon-specific ribosome dwell times, using Variational AutoEncoders.

projects.title: Enhancing Protein Design Through Advanced Graph Neural Networks
projects.summary: Applies advanced graph neural networks to protein design, building on machine learning applications in biology.

projects.title: Development and characterization of an acoustic matched source
projects.summary: Develops and characterizes an acoustic matched source, drawing on nonlinear and time-varying systems in wave engineering. The page excerpt is truncated.

projects.title: VENOVA : an actively modified cylindrical cross-saxophone
projects.summary: Concerns an actively modified cylindrical cross-saxophone, a project described on the page as building on work by a team of engineers from Yamaha. The page excerpt is truncated.

projects.title: Longitudinal Brain Connectomics and Functional Fingerprinting in Chronic Tinnitus
projects.summary: A semester or MSc thesis project investigating how large-scale brain networks reorganize during neurofeedback treatment for chronic tinnitus.

projects.title: Developmental Trajectories of Perinatal Resting-State fMRI dynamics
projects.summary: Investigates the maturation of brain functional dynamics during the perinatal period, for example by applying Co-Activation Pattern (CAP) analysis.

projects.title: Dynamic mode decomposition of fMRI during film watching
projects.summary: Applies dynamic mode decomposition (DMD), a latent space discovery method, to fMRI data acquired during naturalistic film watching.

projects.title: Encoding and Decoding fMRI during film watching
projects.summary: Studies human brain decoding and encoding during naturalistic stimuli, namely film watching, extending prior work on simple images.

projects.title: Community Detection in Directed (Brain) Networks
projects.summary: Aims to develop community detection for directed and asymmetric networks, such as brain networks, rather than symmetric graphs.

projects.title: Investigating memory consolidation during sleep with functional MRI
projects.summary: Uses a dataset of lucid dreamers scanned with fMRI during a hand motor sequence training, both awake and during sleep, to study memory consolidation mechanisms.

projects.title: Graph signal processing to investigate structure-function coupling during sleep
projects.summary: Treats fMRI signals as defined on the structural brain graph to study how functional activity emerges from anatomical fiber bundles during sleep, using graph signal processing.

projects.title: The role of the hippocampus in tracking personal goals
projects.summary: Analyses fMRI scans of healthy subjects performing specific goal-directed tasks to study the role of the hippocampus in distinguishing goals over time.

projects.title: Biophysical Modelling of Microstructural Diffusion MRI in the Rodent Brain
projects.summary: Uses advanced biophysical models of diffusion MRI to extract quantitative maps of brain microstructure in animal models of disease compared with healthy controls. Possible applications mentioned include Parkinson's disease and creatine-related conditions. The page text is truncated.

projects.title: Structural connectivity of the human brain: what can we learn from intracerebral electrophysiological recordings in epileptic patients?
projects.summary: Explores how intracerebral electrophysiological recordings in epileptic patients can inform the structural connectivity of the human brain, using a connectomics framework for healthy and pathological brain data. The page text is truncated.

projects.title: Unraveling the contrast mechanism of neuromelanin-sensitive MRI
projects.summary: Aims to understand the contrast mechanism of neuromelanin-sensitive MRI, a technique that detects pathological alterations in diseases such as Parkinson's disease and schizophrenia. The technique is thought to reflect catecholaminergic function rather than directly measuring neuromelanin. The page text is truncated.

projects.title: Performance Modeling of eBPF Programs
projects.summary: Design a scalable and accurate performance model for eBPF programs, to support performance quantification, debugging, and checking of eBPF kernel extensions against functionally equivalent baselines. The page targets students who want to do a thesis or long-term research.

projects.title: Improving the performance of ML workloads
projects.summary: Analyze and break down the software-stack overheads of ML inference and training, within a single machine and across machines, and propose optimizations to improve system performance.

projects.title: Fused decompression and decoding
projects.summary: Explore fusing decompression with decoding (e.g. gzip+JSON) so that redundant data in the compressed stream is decoded once instead of once per repetition. The page suggests starting with a gzip compressor that places block boundaries at JSON object boundaries.

projects.title: A deduplicating file system based on content-aware chunking
projects.summary: Design a deduplicating file system that splits files into chunks using a content-based hash rather than fixed-size blocks, so that insertions do not destroy deduplication. A follow-up asks how to normalize binaries (e.g. jump targets) in a live file system to improve deduplication.

projects.title: Reducing common sources of branch target aliasing
projects.summary: Explore software and hardware approaches to reduce branch-predictor aliasing caused by common code patterns in lazy-language runtimes and bytecode interpreters, for example by assigning distinct branches to each lazy value or exposing the interpreted program counter to the hardware.

projects.title: Compressed datastructures and application-specific RAM compression
projects.summary: Investigate application-specific compression schemes that are compatible with the operations performed on the decompressed data, keeping existing data structures and applying compression to slices of program data. The example given is compressing the two sides of an Emacs gap buffer separately.

projects.title: Abusing the instruction cache to store data
projects.summary: Encode constant data in the instruction cache through dynamically generated code, so that programs such as SMT solvers can free data-cache pressure. The example replaces a loop adding a constant vector with unrolled code that embeds the constants as immediates.

projects.title: Code-size optimizations for keyboard macros
projects.summary: Design and implement an optimizer that suggests shorter or more ergonomic key combinations for keyboard macros as users type, for example in Emacs or vim. Follow-ups cover physical hand models and aggregated telemetry.

projects.title: Hierarchical rendering of separation-logic formulae
projects.summary: Extend the SepViz system into a hierarchical renderer that nests diagrams and formulae, so that it can display nested predicates such as specifications of higher-order functions, non-prenex quantification, and complex predicates inside iterated separating conjunctions.

projects.title: Mixed rendering for proof presentation
projects.summary: Design a modular constraint-solving based renderer that can mix graphs, pretty-printing, mathematical notation and other visual formats in proof assistant goals, with a notation mechanism in Rocq and a focus on continuity between consecutive proof states.

projects.title: The user experience of mechanized diagram-chasing proofs
projects.summary: Build lightweight mockups of scripted interactions to explore how diagram-chasing proofs should be visualized and manipulated in a proof assistant, including layout, incremental re-layout, and the representation of diagrams.

projects.title: A proof-friendly representation of hardware circuits
projects.summary: Design or identify a circuit representation suitable for use as a compilation target in Rocq that is easy to reason about and supports sharing and optimizations, and use it to retarget the Kôika compiler and reduce its trusted base.

projects.title: Hindley-Milner for Rocq
projects.summary: Extend Rocq's type inference so that it introduces new type variables for remaining holes, enabling simple non-dependently typed definitions such as a generic map function, and study how this approach fails and what errors it produces.

projects.title: Early reclamation for lazy values in Scala
projects.summary: Change the JVM backend of the Scala compiler to null out stack variables right after their last use, so that lazy lists consumed by a function such as foreach can be garbage-collected while being processed.

projects.title: Better unification in Rocq
projects.summary: Make Rocq's unification report failures more eagerly by pinpointing where a naive unification attempt fails, instead of reporting that a whole goal fails to unify with a lemma.

projects.title: Single-step eauto for Rocq
projects.summary: Implement an eauto_one tactic that applies any lemma from a given hint database matching the current goal, replacing an existing complicated trick for extensible forward reasoning.

projects.title: An Alectryon backend for coqdoc
projects.summary: Write a coqdoc backend that generates Alectryon documents, making it easier to switch between the two documentation tools for Rocq.

projects.title: Printing with sharing in Rocq
projects.summary: Add an option, similar to Lisp's *print-circle*, that prints Rocq terms with sharing so that term sizes and memory usage can be analysed more easily when debugging performance issues.

projects.title: Profiling automated verifiers
projects.summary: Build a profiler that attributes SMT solving time to the tasks of the verifier stack (symbolic executor, verifier, solver) and identifies redundant work such as useless quantifier instantiations, evaluated on real verifier performance issues.

projects.title: A different kind of performance profiler
projects.summary: Design a profiler that uses memory snapshots and taint tracking to flag redundant or unused computations, reporting how many distinct results each function computes and whether results are used, to guide memoization and removal of wasted work.

projects.title: Cross-language editing and debugging for legacy code
projects.summary: Write a readable translator from a legacy language such as COBOL into Python, and a reverse translator that back-propagates changes made to the translation to the source. A follow-up proposes back-propagating manual optimizations from assembly to C.

projects.title: Deriving tools from annotated grammars
projects.summary: Enhance a parser generator such as Menhir to accept indentation and other annotations, so that one grammar drives syntax highlighting, indentation, structural editing and folding in editors, with error recovery for partial programs. A follow-up covers grammar-based completion and bounded lookback.

projects.title: Does semantic versioning work?
projects.summary: Study whether human-assigned version numbers follow semantic versioning, using API diffs and downstream test-suite breakage to check consistency, and compare with tools such as semantic-release and automatic enforcement.

projects.title: What performance do compiler updates buy you?
projects.summary: Compile selected historical programs with successive versions of a compiler such as GCC to measure the runtime speedup gained and the increase in compilation time, with a follow-up on which optimizations speed up compiling the compiler itself.

projects.title: PCP encoding for Rocq's VM
projects.summary: Investigate a probabilistically checkable proof (PCP) encoding of traces of Rocq's virtual machine, so that a claimed reduction can be verified cheaply.

projects.title: Alectryon ports to new proof languages
projects.summary: Extend Alectryon to support additional proof languages and protocols, such as F*, HOL-light, or other systems beyond the already supported Rocq and Lean, to compare how communities present their proofs.

projects.title: Fixing reStructuredText
projects.summary: Design and implement a conservative extension of reStructuredText that supports nesting of inline constructs and offers an alternative to heavy indentation for long blocks of text.

projects.title: A collaborative document-annotation system based on reStructuredText
projects.summary: Extend reStructuredText to support inline annotations and discussions that remain robust to document changes, with a single source of truth for the document.

projects.title: Add post-macro-expansion mode to latexdiff
projects.summary: Patch latexdiff to expand simple custom LaTeX macros before running its diff algorithm, so that diffs show the expanded content rather than macro invocations.

projects.title: Static-checking RPG quests
projects.summary: Use automated program verification to prove functional and reachability/liveness properties of role-playing game quests written in modder scripting languages, to detect quests that get stuck, can be completed twice, or lack a reward path.

projects.title: Masters project: AI-based generative approaches for de novo protein design
projects.summary: Develop diffusion generative deep-learning models to design de novo proteins with precise functions for biomedical applications. The student would help integrate physics-based loss functions into the lab's existing deep learning framework.

projects.title: Interpretable and Controllable Neural Shape Parameterizations
projects.summary: Aims to make neural representations of 2D and 3D shapes easier to interpret and control, building on approaches such as DeepGeo that combine neural networks with mesh-based deformation. The page text is truncated.

projects.title: Self-Supervised Learning of Flight Dynamics
projects.summary: Aims to learn how an aircraft responds to control inputs from observation alone, using self-supervised methods such as Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPA), without manually labeled data. The page text is truncated.

projects.title: Structured 3D Shape Optimization with Part-Based Implicit Neural Representations
projects.summary: Develops structured, modular and optimizable 3D shape representations for engineering design, using a part-based implicit neural representation that decodes latent vectors and poses into shape parts. The page text is truncated.

projects.title: Recovering Thin Structures in 3D Foundation Models
projects.summary: Investigates how to improve 3D foundation models, which predict scene geometry and camera parameters with transformers, so that they recover thin structures that current patch-based designs handle poorly. The page text is truncated.

projects.title: Applied Deep Learning for Computer Aided Engineering
projects.summary: Aims to use deep learning to automate Computer Aided Engineering (CAE) workflows in industrial engineering and manufacturing, reducing time and human resource costs and R&D expenses.

projects.title: Real-Time 3D Tracking and Anomaly Detection for Maritime Kite Systems
projects.summary: For Aether Swiss Kite, aims to build a 360° vision-based redundancy system for real-time 3D kite tracking and anomaly detection, extending a previous semester project that achieved 2D detection, trajectory mapping and orientation tracking. The page text is truncated.

projects.title: Efficient Diffusion Models via Quantization and Compression
projects.summary: Aims to explore and systematically evaluate quantization and compression methods for diffusion models such as Stable Diffusion, to make them efficient enough for resource-constrained devices. The page text is truncated.

projects.title: 3D Surface reconstruction using 3D Gaussians and SDF
projects.summary: Aims to reconstruct 3D surfaces by combining 3D Gaussian Splatting with signed distance functions (SDF), building on methods such as SuGaR that adapt Gaussian splatting for surface reconstruction. The page text is truncated.

projects.title: Computer Vision for Waste Management (CVLab x Wasteflow)
projects.summary: A computer vision project for waste management, offered jointly by CVLab and Wasteflow. The page gives no further description.

projects.title: 3D Surface reconstruction using 3D Gaussians and SDF
projects.summary: The project aims to build primitives so that a surface can be obtained from a 3D Gaussian scene with minimal extra computational cost, building on methods such as SuGaR and hybrid approaches that train a neural SDF alongside 3D Gaussians. Objectives are a literature review and experiments with different SDF formulations.

projects.title: Real-Time 3D Tracking and Anomaly Detection for Maritime Kite Systems
projects.summary: Integrate and calibrate a second camera to build a stereovision setup for 3D tracking of an automated kite wing used for maritime propulsion. The project then moves to real-time hardware processing, anomaly detection (e.g. tears, abnormal trajectories), and linking vision outputs to safety control actions.

projects.title: Applied Deep Learning for Computer Aided Engineering
projects.summary: Students work on one of CVLab's deep learning problems for computer-aided engineering in aeronautics, such as object geometry parameterization, surrogate modeling of physical performance, or gradient-based optimization. The work is done in collaboration with aerodynamics experts at ISAE-SUPAERO.

projects.title: Applying Machine Learning to 4D/5D Neuroimaging Data to Advance Motor Control Research
projects.summary: Develop a machine learning approach to identify and reconstruct each individual neuron in large 4D/5D neuroimaging datasets, using the time axis (neural dynamics) to improve segmentation compared with 3D U-net pipelines. The project is a collaboration with the Neuroengineering Lab, which provides the datasets from limb-movement control experiments.

projects.title: Computer Vision for Waste Management
projects.summary: Develop a computer vision solution for WasteFlow's SaaS that helps recycling facilities characterize waste mix, measure sorting efficiency, and detect performance loss. Possible tasks include real-time detection and classification of waste on conveyor belts, mass estimation, purity assessment, and foreign material identification, with optional deployment on edge devices.

projects.title: Digging into the Transformers of 3D Foundation Model
projects.summary: The project studies the transformer components of VGGT, a feed-forward 3D foundation model that predicts scene geometry and camera parameters from many images. The goal is to understand how these transformers work and to devise better algorithms that make the model faster and more accurate.

projects.title: Efficient Diffusion Models via Quantization and Compression
projects.summary: The project aims to explore and systematically evaluate quantization and compression methods (INT8/INT4, mixed-precision, pruning, low-rank factorization, distillation) for diffusion models such as Stable Diffusion. The goal is to reduce computational and memory requirements while preserving generative quality, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices.

projects.title: Interpretable and Controllable Neural Shape Parameterizations
projects.summary: The project aims to build on DeepGeo to develop methods that make neural shape parameterizations more interpretable, controllable, and efficient to optimize. Research questions include automatically constructing parameter directions for geometric properties (e.g. airfoil thickness, camber, wing twist), keeping controls reliable under large deformations, and designing compact, adaptive parameter spaces that improve optimization convergence.

projects.title: Proton Irradiation of Nvidia GPU
projects.summary: The student will support proton irradiation experiments on an Nvidia Jetson Orin NX running a machine learning algorithm, at the Paul Scherrer Institute. The work includes test runs, logging and analysing single-event-effect bit flips, and validating the results against simulations.

projects.title: Recovering Thin Structures in 3D Foundation Models
projects.summary: The project aims to improve the performance of transformer-based 3D foundation models, such as Depth Anything 3, on thin structures, which are poorly handled due to the rough patchification of transformers. The student will investigate how to improve the model's performance on these thin structures.

projects.title: Self-Supervised Learning of Flight Dynamics
projects.summary: The research project aims to explore self-supervised methods, such as Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPA), for learning aircraft dynamics from sensor measurements, with a focus on making the learned models useful for control. The student will propose and test new approaches on simulated flight data and potentially real measurements from the lab's experimental aircraft.

projects.title: Structured 3D Shape Optimization with Part-Based Implicit Neural Representations
projects.summary: The project aims to extend the part-based implicit representation PartSDF to engineering-driven 3D shape representation and optimization under constraints. Goals include structured multi-part representations, enforcing physical and design constraints (e.g. aerodynamics or structural efficiency), and scalable architectures for many-part objects.

projects.title: Web development for graphic music analysis app
projects.summary: Develop the web interface of the lab's reductive music analysis app, which lets researchers express music analyses as graphs embedded in MEI music scores. Students can either rewrite the serverless web app in type-safe code with a modern event-driven JavaScript framework, or add features and fix bugs in the existing legacy code base.

projects.title: Perceptual abilities of musical experts
projects.summary: Replicate existing behavioural music perception experiments with top-level performing artists to test how their perceptual abilities differ from those of previously studied participants. The project involves critically updating the original study's methods, implementing an online version, and analysing the data.

projects.title: Testing & Quality Assurance (C++ & Python) - LARS
projects.summary: Improve the reliability and maintainability of the LARS real-time interactive music system by designing a comprehensive test suite (unit, integration, regression, load tests) for its C++ and Python components. The project also includes setting up CI automated testing workflows and defining testing standards for plugins.

projects.title: Python Utilities to C++ Core Migration - LARS
projects.summary: Move key utilities of the LARS system from Python to optimized modern C++, including the C++ version of its pattern language for algorithmic composition. The work includes testing and benchmarking the translated code and maintaining the Python bindings via nanobind.

projects.title: Performance Optimization & Benchmarking - LARS
projects.summary: Improve the real-time performance and scalability of the LARS system by profiling it, optimizing critical C++ code paths, and addressing threading and concurrency issues. The project also involves building benchmarking tools and automating performance regression tests.

projects.title: Audio Processing - LARS
projects.summary: Add audio capabilities to the LARS real-time music system, including computing hardware delays and extracting audio features such as beat tracking and key finding. The project requires signal processing and low-latency real-time programming skills.

projects.title: Coercion-resistant proof of personhood as a foundation for digital democracy
projects.summary: Prototype, test, and evaluate a coercion-resistance mechanism for e-voting in the context of in-person pseudonym parties, including a barebones web or mobile app and an informal usability study with volunteers. The goal is a detailed report, ideally leading to a research paper.

projects.title: Paradox-resistant reasoning in automated theorem provers
projects.summary: Help formalize, validate, and metalogically reason about Grounded Deduction, a non-classical logic foundation that allows unrestricted recursive definitions while defusing semantic paradoxes. Work uses a proof assistant or automated theorem prover such as Isabelle, Coq, or Lean, and optionally a grounded set theory in the LISA prover.

projects.title: Writing and editing tools based on matchertext and MinML
projects.summary: Develop tools and refine the MinML markup language, which is based on the matchertext syntactic discipline for cross-language embedding. Possible work includes integrating MinML authoring into existing Web and other tools, or designing a LaTeX-like MinML document language.

projects.title: Preparing and Evaluating Vintage Language Models
projects.summary: Prepare the methodological and technical foundations for Vintage LLMs, language models trained only on pre-modern historical corpora. The work covers corpus construction, contamination control, synthetic data and historically grounded evaluation benchmarks.

projects.title: Temporal Language Models and the Dynamics of Language Change
projects.summary: Study and extend temporal language model approaches inspired by TLM-1 to model semantic drift, narrative evolution and temporal forecasting. The work uses diachronic corpora such as newspapers, books or archives.

projects.title: Discovering Historical Events Through Spatio-Temporal Analysis
projects.summary: Design and prototype a reproducible, unsupervised spatiotemporal anomaly-detection pipeline that surfaces historically significant events in the Flickr Commons archive. The project is carried out with the Flickr Foundation.

projects.title: Pleiades Integration into the TimeAtlas
projects.summary: Design and prototype the integration of the Pleiades gazetteer of ancient places into the Time Atlas infrastructure. The work includes data mapping, ingestion pipelines and visualization of ancient places.

projects.title: IIIF Document Information Extraction for Time Atlas
projects.summary: Build a pipeline that fetches manuscript images through IIIF, transcribes and structures them with language-vision models, and extracts named entities and spatiotemporal information. The results are prepared for integration into Time Atlas.

projects.title: Geolocating Artworks
projects.summary: Develop methods that use vision-language models and multimodal embeddings to identify the places depicted in paintings, engravings and illustrations. The goal is to link artworks to spatial entities in the Time Atlas.

projects.title: News Articles in Space and Time
projects.summary: A semester project on news articles in space and time. The page gives only the title and states that the description is coming soon.

projects.title: Preparing Historical Data for Apertus
projects.summary: Collect, filter, clean, normalize and document historical and cultural heritage corpora for a future training cycle of the open Apertus language model. The work covers OCR quality, metadata, deduplication and contamination filtering.

projects.title: EPFL Digital Twin Foundation Model
projects.summary: Prototype a first foundation model of the EPFL campus by aligning heterogeneous datasets (3D structures, occupancy, food, mobility, schedules) into a unified spatiotemporal representation. The model is intended for forecasting and counterfactual simulation.

projects.title: Bias analysis of cultural heritage manipulation classification of Wikipedia edits by LLMs
projects.summary: Analyse biases of open-source LLMs when classifying Wikipedia edits about Armenian and Ukrainian cultural heritage as manipulative, using a human-labelled ground truth. The project also explores bias mitigation strategies such as prompt engineering and multi-agent setups.

projects.title: EpiDoc Corpus Creation & Geolocation (ArmEpiC)
projects.summary: One of four coordinated semester projects in the ArmEpiC initiative, which structures the Armenian epigraphic corpus of India (IndiaArmEpiC) in TEI/EpiDoc. This project covers corpus creation and geolocation.

projects.title: AI-Assisted Authority Files & Validation Dashboard (ArmEpiC)
projects.summary: One of four coordinated semester projects in the ArmEpiC initiative, on AI-assisted workflows for authority files and a validation dashboard for the Armenian epigraphic data.

projects.title: Standalone Web Visualisation (ArmEpiC)
projects.summary: One of four coordinated semester projects in the ArmEpiC initiative, on a standalone web visualisation of the Armenian epigraphic data.

projects.title: Armenian Editorial Signs Converter (ArmEpiC)
projects.summary: One of four coordinated semester projects in the ArmEpiC initiative, on converting Armenian editorial signs in the epigraphic data.

projects.title: Dense Language Encoders for Agglomerative Models
projects.summary: Build a dense text encoder that aligns language with the dense features of agglomerative vision models such as EUPE. The goal is zero-shot open-vocabulary semantic segmentation by cosine similarity.

projects.title: World Model Semantic Surprise as a Measure for Multimodal Urban Incongruity
projects.summary: Develop embedding-space semantic trajectory tools and apply them to urban trajectories from driving videos, street-view imagery, LiDAR or building text. The aim is to measure violation of expectation as an indicator of urban incongruity.

projects.title: Reconstructing the Past: Generating 3D Models of Lost Buildings from Stylistically Diverse Inputs with Geometry Transformers
projects.summary: Test feed-forward geometry transformers (MapAnything, VGGT, NOVA3R) on natural and stylized images, then fine-tune the best model. The final aim is to generate 3D models of lost buildings from DHLAB historical image collections.

projects.title: 3D Question Answering at City-Scale: Multimodal LLMs
projects.summary: Implement a 3D multimodal LLM for question answering over city-scale 3D models using aligned historical data from Time Atlas. The model is to be integrated into the Time Atlas software.

projects.title: Converging Conceptual Abstraction in Self-Supervised Models
projects.summary: Develop a representation-convergence technique that compares the conceptual abstractions learned by sparse autoencoders or cross-layer transcoders across self-supervised models. The project examines transfer of these abstractions between models.

projects.title: Driving Representation Convergence using Image Aesthetics
projects.summary: Test whether aesthetic images produce representations and representational geometry distinct from non-aesthetic images, and whether aesthetics drives cross-model convergence. The project includes building an international, historically balanced aesthetics dataset.

projects.title: Tarot Deck Motif Analysis
projects.summary: Prepare the corpus, data model and an initial taxonomy of visual motifs for analysing historical Tarot decks, and prototype computer-vision tools to detect and classify recurring motifs. The project is run with the University of Lausanne.

projects.title: Spatial Intelligence at Scale: Implicit Reconstruction
projects.summary: Prepare datasets and pipelines and research neural reconstruction methods for egocentric semantic understanding, as part of a SwissAI-funded open-vocabulary 3D model for city-scale scenes. The page mentions extending the VGGT paradigm.

projects.title: Spatial Intelligence at Scale: Hierarchical Reconstruction
projects.summary: Investigate methods for creating object-part hierarchies in city-scale 3D data, derived from per-point open-vocabulary labels, including hyperbolic embeddings. It is part of a SwissAI-funded project.

projects.title: Spatial Intelligence at Scale: Human Interaction

projects.title: The Social Life of Images: Using Social Metadata to Enhance AI Generated Descriptions of Digital Image Archives

projects.summary: Build a bilingual (Armenian-English) dataset of culturally embedded expressions, annotated with the PSCM schema. The annotated data is used to evaluate LLM and MT performance on culture-specific meaning.

projects.title: Tracking the Weaponization and Manipulation of Cultural Heritage in Armenia
projects.summary: Retrieve and analyse Wikipedia editing histories, talk pages and related content to monitor how cultural heritage narratives about Armenia are manipulated. Findings are intended to support documentation and heritage protection.

projects.title: Detection, Linking, and Georeferencing of Place Names in Historical Newspapers
projects.summary: Scale multilingual location detection and georeferencing, with a focus on sub-city levels, across the Impresso historical newspaper corpus. The work includes relevance filtering and evaluation.

projects.title: What's in those millions of images? Generating accurate descriptions for 4 million historical newspaper images
projects.summary: Generate and evaluate textual descriptions of roughly 4 million Impresso newspaper images by comparing vision-language models. The work includes building a test set and defining evaluation criteria.

projects.title: VLM Finetuning for Accurate Features from Images of Degraded Point Clouds
projects.summary: Evaluate how base vision-language models perform on synthetic renderings of sparse point clouds versus real images, then fine-tune them to produce embeddings closer to those of real images.

projects.title: Projecting Representations of Beauty
projects.summary: Build a pseudo-labelling pipeline that projects aesthetic labels from image assessment models onto 3D scenes, and train a model to predict aesthetic labels from point cloud structure alone.

projects.title: Biology of a VLM: Transcoder Training for Multimodal Interpretability
projects.summary: Train a transcoder replacement model for a vision-language model and use it to analyse the model's internal reasoning, including modality-unified concept features and reasoning on text-heavy documents.

projects.title: Armenian Epigraphy and Cultural Heritage Data Analysis
projects.summary: Collect and clean a selection of books on epigraphy and cultural heritage, store them in a database, and extract key terms and themes with NLP techniques, with a focus on Armenian inscriptions.

projects.title: Identification and Classification of Maps in Historical Newspapers
projects.summary: Train a binary map vs. non-map image classifier on Impresso newspaper pages, then a classifier for the country or region a map represents. The page states an annotated dataset for the first step already exists.

projects.title: Tracking the Weaponization and Manipulation of Cultural Heritage in Ukraine by Russia
projects.summary: Analyse Wikipedia editing histories, talk pages and content about Ukrainian cultural heritage to monitor politically motivated manipulation. Findings are intended to support heritage protection and policy.

projects.title: Exploring Large Vision Models for Historical Newspaper Segmentation
projects.summary: Evaluate large vision models for segmenting and labelling logical layout units (titles, text paragraphs, tables, images) on historical newspaper pages from the Impresso corpus.

projects.title: Evaluating the Novelty of Knowledge in Texts with Large Language Models
projects.summary: Develop algorithms that assess whether historical texts contain knowledge that was not already present in an LLM's pretraining data. The work combines novelty detection with retrieval approaches.

projects.summary: Extract the semi-structured information of Fritz Blaser's Swiss Press Bibliography (1956) into a lightweight database describing Swiss newspapers from 1803 to 1958. The database supports the Impresso web application and studies of the Swiss press.

projects.title: Analysing Layout Elements of Historical Maps
projects.summary: Detect map layout elements such as cartouches, scale bars, wind roses and illustrations in a dataset of about 400,000 historical maps, then cluster them by author, region and period.

projects.title: Cost models & tuning the query optimizer of a JIT analytical engine
projects.summary: The student will become familiar with Apache Calcite and model the cost of the operators of Proteus, an in-house analytical DBMS engine. The goal is cost models that let the optimizer reason about parallelization and resource allocation, and an auto-tuning infrastructure to select cost-model hyper-parameters for different machines. The project lasts 14 weeks.

projects.title: Limiting interference of code generation to analytical query execution through remote JIT-ing
projects.summary: The project studies how just-in-time code generation interferes with analytical query execution in the Proteus DBMS, and quantifies the resulting slowdown. It then explores running code generation remotely on a separate, possibly smaller machine to isolate it from query execution, measuring the effect on query latency and throughput. The project is 14 weeks long.

projects.title: Efficient Concurrent Interval Container for Multicore Systems
projects.summary: Design and implement a concurrent interval container inspired by the Boost Interval Container Library, with an index layout and synchronization protocol supporting concurrent overlap and containment queries and atomic updates. The prototype will be evaluated against a global-lock sequential container and concurrent-index baselines on throughput, latency, scalability and memory.

projects.title: Understanding and Mitigating Real-World Global Serializability Violations
projects.summary: The project studies global serializability violations in multi-database transactions of microservice applications. The student will empirically study 2-3 open-source microservice applications, integrate existing mitigation methods (e.g. Sonata, the Ticket method, ad hoc synchronization), and evaluate their performance.

projects.title: Memory-Aware Hash Joins for Heterogeneous Memory Environments
projects.summary: The project studies the design space of hash join implementations in heterogeneous memory environments such as CXL memory. The student will evaluate existing hash joins, analyze the design space, and propose memory-aware hash join design choices evaluated on SSB and TPC-H.

projects.title: Cross-Query Reuse for Efficient Semantic Query Processing
projects.summary: Design, implement, and evaluate a reuse layer for semantic query processing over unstructured data with LLM-based operators. The project combines caching of operator results, grouping of queries into shared LLM calls, and deriving answers for new conditions from earlier results, within a cost-based optimizer. Duration is 4-6 months.

projects.title: Three-Dimensional UWB Localization for Heterogeneous Ground–Aerial Robot Teams
projects.summary: Extend an existing Webots simulation framework for UWB localization, in which ground anchors localize mobile tags, to aerial mobile tags. The work covers 3D estimation algorithms, LOS/NLOS measurement models, and evaluation of accuracy and robustness; a master project may add hardware-in-the-loop and motion-capture experiments.

projects.title: Cooperative Gas Source Localization with Infrastructure-Free UWB Positioning
projects.summary: Investigate cooperative gas source localization with heterogeneous robot teams whose positions come from infrastructure-free UWB relative localization. The student builds a simplified 2D simulated gas environment, implements a cooperative source estimation algorithm, and evaluates it with ground-truth, noisy and UWB-estimated robot positions.

projects.title: Robotic Gas Sensor Calibration
projects.summary: Design an efficient pre-flight calibration setup for low-cost gas sensors (MOX and PID) on a quadcopter, so that absolute gas concentration can be estimated despite slow sensor dynamics and dependence on temperature and humidity. The setup integrates temperature, humidity, flow and gas sensors with a pump, valve and quadcopter.

projects.title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Gas Source Localization
projects.summary: Extend an existing reinforcement learning approach for gas source localization (DDPG, SAC) to a multi-robot system using multi-agent RL. The project studies which information agents should exchange, how to remain robust to communication limits such as packet drops, and how to compress messages.

projects.title: Asymmetric Multi-modal Deep Vision Model Compression
projects.summary: Reduce the memory footprint, inference time and energy cost of RGB-thermal deep vision networks for onboard robotic deployment, using pruning and quantization. The project also studies whether the RGB and thermal modalities differ in robustness to compression.

projects.title: Thermal Burst Imaging for Optical Gas Imaging
projects.summary: Increase the signal of thermal image frames captured by a moving camera through burst imaging, using dense image matching that is robust to dynamic scenes, so that weak signals such as gas leaks can be detected. The project can use classical variational methods, learned methods, or a combination.

projects.title: Robust indoor–outdoor state estimation for a compact multirotor
projects.summary: Design a fusion strategy that keeps position estimates continuous and accurate when a compact MAV flies between outdoor and indoor spaces, combining multi-camera visual-inertial odometry (OpenVINS) with GNSS on PX4. The student measures behaviour in real flights with ground truth, reproduces degradations in Webots, and may study camera prioritization; a master project may add AprilTag position anchors.

projects.title: Comparing PSO and Reinforcement Learning for Training Robot Controllers
projects.summary: Fairly compare Particle Swarm Optimization and reinforcement learning when both train the same feedforward neural network controller on a multi-robot benchmark. The project includes a literature review, implementation of both algorithms in a high-fidelity simulator, and analysis of the solutions found under comparable evaluation budgets.

projects.title: Active Sound Source Localization and Ego-Noise Mitigation for Mobile Robots
projects.summary: Develop an onboard acoustic localization framework in which a mobile robot with a microphone array localizes sound sources despite its own motor and wheel noise. The project covers ego-noise characterization and suppression, multi-channel localization (GCC-PHAT, SRP-PHAT or trilateration) for 360° azimuth and proximity estimation, and deployment on real hardware.

projects.title: Vision-Language Uncertainty Maps for Drone Search
projects.summary: Build a map of where a target is likely to be, with per-cell uncertainty, by combining a satellite-image prior scored by a vision-language model with in-flight drone detections. The method is to be benchmarked in simulation on satellite images with known target locations, and optionally used to decide when to ask the operator for clarification.

projects.title: Multi-Robot Inspection with ToF-Based Replanning
projects.summary: Detect, cell by cell, where an inspected asset differs from its prior voxel map using onboard Time-of-Flight depth frames, and replan viewpoints and task assignments for a team of MAVs accordingly. The approach is to be evaluated in Webots on modified assets and, if time allows, with real MAVs.

projects.summary: The project aims to develop approaches that describe satellite images and their changes in natural language, producing explanations accessible to non-experts. It combines machine learning for Earth observation with knowledge from large textual corpora such as Wikipedia and specialized web pages, in collaboration with the NLP lab.

projects.title: AI for topographic mapping
projects.summary: Develop new AI models that are robust and effective in real-world scenarios for land cover and land use mapping from satellite and aerial imagery. The work targets three challenges: hard-to-delimit class boundaries, incorporating multi-modal data such as text and ground-level images, and model interpretability.

projects.title: An AI assistant to interact with remote sensing images
projects.summary: Develop a natural-language interface that lets non-expert users ask questions in English about satellite images and receive answers in English. The work targets remote sensing visual question answering and aims to make the reasoning behind answers transparent and interpretable. The project is carried out with the Φ-lab at the European Space Agency and the Université de Paris Cité.

projects.summary: The project addresses the issue of limited labeled data in very high resolution aerial imagery. It aims to learn change-detection models efficiently in this setting. The project is a partnership with AXA.

projects.title: Generative Workflow for Navigable 3D Worlds from a Large-Scale Panoramic Painting
projects.summary: Develop a reproducible generative AI workflow that turns segments of a large panoramic painting (the 1893 Murten Panorama) into navigable 3D scenes using world models and 3D asset generation, with scenes placed on a geolocated terrain map for VR/XR heritage experiences.
skills: generative AI tools for images and 3D

projects.title: Beyond the Strings: LLM-Based Knowledge Extraction for Historical Puppetry Knowledge Graphs
projects.summary: Evaluate LLM-based extraction of historical relationships and scholarly interpretations from a small corpus of theatrical and archival texts on Sophie Taeuber-Arp's 1918 König Hirsch marionettes, comparing how models separate historical facts from interpretations and map them to a predefined ontology for knowledge graphs.

projects.title: Evaluation Framework for Cross-Domain Visual Retrieval in Cultural Heritage Image Collections
projects.summary: Build a rigorous, reproducible evaluation framework for cross-domain visual retrieval and UMAP-based visualization tools applied to cultural heritage image collections, including the Murten Panorama and 15th-century manuscripts. The work covers dataset survey, generative construction of evaluation sets, and benchmarking of retrieval accuracy and visualization fidelity.

projects.title: Tracking Novel Research Through the Publication Process: A Text-Embedding Approach
projects.summary: Study scientific conservatism in peer review by measuring the novelty of submitted manuscripts with text embedding models. The student reviews embedding models for semantic similarity and builds a framework matching rejected papers to their eventual publications, using anonymized manuscript and peer review data from more than 2,000 Elsevier journals via the ICSR Lab.

projects.title: Measuring Entrepreneurial and Industry Identity in the Asteroid-Mining Industry with NLP
projects.summary: Analyse how entrepreneurs and institutions describe themselves as the asteroid-mining industry takes shape. The student builds an NLP pipeline that collects longitudinal text data (including Internet Archive company websites, communications, interviews and media) and a machine learning model separating general topics, individual identity claims and collective industry claims, validated against a manually annotated sample.

projects.title: Microarchitectural explorations for biomedical applications
projects.summary: Explore whether an in-order superscalar RISC-V core (CV32E20) instead of the current single-issue core in X-HEEP can improve energy efficiency for the BiomedBench biomedical wearable applications. The student will build a lightweight RISC-V simulator, generate execution traces, model superscalar execution, and later assess power overheads.

projects.title: Tencer Metamaterials: Unit Cell Generation and Rigid Motion Analysis
projects.summary: Design new classes of mechanical metamaterial unit cells built from tencers (tension-constrained elastic rods). The student will develop an automatic tool that generates diverse candidate unit-cell topologies for simulation, and a strategy to refine designs so that no undesired relative rigid motion is possible between components.

projects.title: Inverse design of highly curved surfaces for surface-based inflatables
projects.summary: The project aims to develop a parameterization method for highly curved surfaces that respects the contraction bounds of surface-based inflatables by using cone singularities. Key questions include optimizing cone placement and angles under scale-factor bounds, realizing the resulting cuts physically, and measuring how much the achievable shape range is extended compared with existing methods.

projects.title: Computational Design with Multiple Tension Elements: Elastic Cables and Sheets with Elastic Rod Structures
projects.summary: The project studies how cables and sheet patches can be treated as interchangeable and combinable tension elements that shape elastic rods into target curves. The student will build on an existing cable-to-patch conversion prototype and a C++/Python framework, addressing open questions on form-finding, evaluation, intersection-free layout and topology optimization.

projects.title: Simulation and Design of Transformable Elastic Linkages
projects.summary: Explore how elastic beams and joints can be designed and connected to achieve desired transformations, shapes, and functions, such as deployable shells and grid-shell-like structures (X-Shell, C-Shell, BamX). The work aims to simulate the behaviour of elastic linkage systems and develop new ones guided by geometric insight, combining parametric modeling, physics-based simulation, numerical optimization, inverse design and possibly physical prototyping. Students may propose their own research directions.

projects.title: Dynamic Frequency Allocation for Speech Separation
projects.summary: Investigates whether speech separation models such as TIGER should allocate frequency resolution dynamically per input mixture while keeping computational cost fixed. Includes analysis of per-utterance performance across fixed frequency partitions and a possible lightweight predictor of frequency allocation, with attention to pathological speech.

projects.title: Efficient Robot Data Collection through Geometric Shared Autonomy
projects.summary: Extends the GeoSACS interface, which represents task structure with a canal surface and lets users correct trajectories with a low-dimensional joystick, into a synchronized multimodal data-recording pipeline for robot manipulation. The project compares its data collection efficiency with conventional teleoperation and prepares datasets for imitation learning.

projects.title: Assessing Lyrics-Based Item Profiles for Music Information Retrieval
projects.summary: Studies whether text-based item profiles built from lyrics and lyric-related resources give more task-relevant representations than direct lyric embeddings for MIR tasks such as genre classification, mood or tag prediction, and retrieval.

projects.title: A Cross-Cultural Study of Podcasts for Well-Being Information Dissemination
projects.summary: Examines how health and well-being topics are framed in podcasts across cultural and language contexts, combining NLP analysis of podcast metadata and transcripts with grounded theory, and relating framing choices to audience engagement.

projects.title: Faithful Vision-Language Explanations for Unified Face Attack Detection
projects.summary: Aims to build a face attack (presentation attack and deepfake) detector paired with a vision-language model that produces explanations, plus a verifier that tests whether generated claims are faithful by perturbing the claimed evidence. The work targets cross-dataset and unseen attack evaluation.

projects.title: From Scientific Data to Citizen Communication: Weather Nowcasting in Malabo, Equatorial Guinea
projects.summary: Aims to build an end-to-end machine-learning pipeline for short-term torrential rain nowcasting in Malabo using open data, integrating a local weather station, and a basic text-based alert system tested in a real scenario, in collaboration with local partners.

projects.title: Adapting foundation models for knowledge transfer in out-of-distribution medical data
projects.summary: Develops adaptive fine-tuning methods for foundation models that reduce performance disparities under distribution shift in medical data, along with benchmarks and evaluation protocols for drift detection and equity-performance trade-offs.

projects.title: Advancing CT-Based Characterization of Poorly Understood Vascular Diseases Through Foundation Models
projects.summary: Aims to develop an interpretable computer-aided diagnostic tool for fibromuscular dysplasia in renal arteries from CTA scans, using segmentation of renal arteries and classification of lesions with machine learning, in collaboration with Idiap and CHUV.

projects.title: Multimodal Learning for Automated Grading of Retinal Inflammation in Dynamic Imaging
projects.summary: Aims to design and validate multimodal machine learning models that automatically detect and grade retinal inflammation from fluorescein angiography images and videos, and to identify interpretable imaging biomarkers.

projects.title: Pseudo labeling of Sensitive Attributes in Medical Imaging for Demographically Fair Machine Learning
projects.summary: Develops machine learning models that pseudo-label sensitive attributes such as gender or age in medical imaging datasets lacking such annotations, and assesses the impact of these pseudo-labels on fairness and performance.

projects.title: Towards Scalable and Interpretable Foundation Models for physiologicals signals recorded during human sleep
projects.summary: Aims to develop self-supervised pretraining strategies for polysomnographic and EEG signals, then fine-tune and evaluate the encoders on sleep staging and seizure detection, including cross-dataset generalization.

projects.title: Agentic retrieval augmented generation interface for sleep Medicine
projects.summary: Focuses on building a Scientific Literature Agent using retrieval-augmented generation over sleep scoring guidelines and medical literature, integrating it with a central LLM and a GUI demonstrator for clinicians (OmniSleep project).

projects.title: From Audiobooks to Character Utterances: Automatic Annotation of Speakers in Literary Fiction
projects.summary: Aims to build a pipeline that automatically annotates speech utterances from LibriVox dramatic-reading audiobooks with their speaking character, to create a large annotated dataset for quotation attribution in fiction.

projects.title: From Personal Stories to Collective Narratives: Computational Analysis of Health Narratives in Podcasts
projects.summary: Aims to develop a computational framework that automatically identifies personal health narratives in podcast transcripts and clusters them to reveal recurring narrative themes.

projects.title: Whole-Body Manipulation with Explicit Self-Balancing Control for Humanoid Robots
projects.summary: Aims to develop a whole-body control strategy for a humanoid robot (Unitree G1) that jointly treats balance and manipulation, accounting for the mass and inertia of arms and manipulated objects. Part of the work may be carried out on-site at S3C in Biel.

projects.title: Robotics: Automated discovery of material properties using dextrous manipulation, vision tools, and learning agents.
projects.summary: Aims to develop a classification framework for solid and semi-solid materials in automated sampling workflows using the FR3 and UR3e robots, vision, and force-torque or rheological cues to identify properties such as viscosity, adhesiveness, cohesiveness and granularity.

projects.title: Design of robotic teleoperation interface
projects.summary: Aims to design a web-based teleoperation interface for the Lio robot, covering navigation, manipulation, and speech, to support public demonstrations and assistive-robotics design studies with caregivers and users.

projects.title: Gaze-Guided Shared Autonomy for Object Manipulation
