projects.summary: Aims to add eye gaze as a source of user intent to a joystick-based shared autonomy framework for object manipulation, fusing gaze with joystick input to predict intent earlier and more accurately, especially in cluttered scenes.

projects.title: Cognitive architecture for assistive robots
projects.summary: Aims to integrate the Lio robot with the DIARC cognitive architecture from Tufts HRILab, connecting it to ROS and developing human-robot interaction demos.

projects.title: Scaling Pre-training for Gaze Following
projects.summary: Aims to pre-train gaze following models on large curated video datasets using pseudo-annotations from strong gaze following models, then fine-tune and evaluate them on annotated video datasets.

projects.title: Spatio-temporal Modeling of Human Behavior in Videos
projects.summary: Explores spatio-temporal video encoders trained end-to-end to extract features for facial behavior tasks such as head gesture and facial expression recognition, with possible weakly-supervised joint learning from pseudo-annotations.

projects.title: Research Spotlight: Crafting An Interactive Webpage Template for Showcasing Science
projects.summary: Aims to create a versatile, feature-rich webpage template for showcasing research papers, including interactive elements for model demonstrations, and to evaluate tools such as Streamlit and Gradio for this purpose.

projects.title: Person Head Detection
projects.summary: Aims to compile public head-annotated datasets and train and evaluate an object detector that localizes whole human heads, with data augmentation for extreme head poses, packaged as a reusable inference pipeline for gaze tracking and head pose estimation.

projects.title: From Gaze Following to Joint Attention
projects.summary: Trains and evaluates a transformer-based gaze following model on a new dataset, measuring gaze following and joint attention, then extends the architecture to predict joint attention end-to-end, in collaboration with the University of Zurich.

projects.title: Parametric Gaze Following
projects.summary: Explores casting gaze following as prediction of a parametric probability distribution (e.g. mixture of Gaussians) instead of a heatmap, and proposes new metrics that capture more information about the predicted distribution.

projects.title: Pathological speech enhancement
projects.summary: Examines the performance of state-of-the-art speech enhancement approaches on pathological speech (e.g. hearing loss, head and neck cancers, neurological disorders), and develops approaches targeting pathological speech if time permits.

projects.title: Pathological speech detection in adverse environments
projects.summary: Examines how state-of-the-art automatic speech processing approaches for diagnosing motor speech disorders perform under noise and reverberation typical of clinical recordings, and develops targeted approaches if relevant.

projects.title: Automatic speech recognition of air-traffic communication using grammar
projects.summary: Aims to build a baseline ASR system for air-traffic controllers in Kaldi and to explore context-free grammar language modeling based on ICAO phraseology, either replacing or enriching statistical language models.

projects.title: Error correction in speech recognition using large pre-trained language models
projects.summary: Investigates whether large pre-trained language models can correct errors in speech transcription output, analysing error types and comparing traditional and conversational language models, including rescoring of N-best hypotheses.

projects.title: Speech/Music Classification
projects.summary: Aims to develop a classifier that discriminates speech from music and possibly noise, starting from an evaluation of existing speech/music and voice activity detection approaches on established data.

projects.title: Speaker identification enhanced by the social network analyser
projects.summary: Aims to build a speaker identification baseline and a graph/network analysis tool, then combine speech and network information to improve person identification on simulated lawful-investigation data, using open-source tools such as SpeechBrain and SocNetV.

projects.title: Automatic named entity recognition from speech
projects.summary: Aims to improve recognition of named entities directly from speech by training the speech recognition and named entity recognition modules together end-to-end, and comparing this with independently trained modules.

projects.title: Punctuation restoration on automatic speech recognition output
projects.summary: Aims to train a model that adds punctuation, and optionally capitalization, to ASR output to improve readability and usefulness for downstream tasks, evaluated on several languages and real scenarios.

projects.title: Social media and crowdsourcing for social good
projects.summary: Offers several student projects within a multidisciplinary initiative on social media analytics, visualization of social and crowdsourced data, and smartphone apps for mobile crowdsourcing, with collaborators in Europe and the Majority World.

projects.title: Understanding the robustness of machine learning models on underspecified tasks
projects.summary: Studies how in-distribution and out-of-distribution performance of deep learning models evolves during pre-training and fine-tuning, aiming to develop model selection strategies for robust models and produce results suitable for a scientific publication.

projects.title: Audiovisual person recognition
projects.summary: Aims to combine audio and visual biometric person identification systems, either by developing them separately and fusing their outputs or by building a single system taking both embeddings as input, building on Idiap's NIST SRE 2019 scripts.

projects.title: An open-source framework for the quantification of Urban Heat Islands in Switzerland
projects.summary: Aims to build an open-source Python or C++ framework that converts Swiss open datasets into inputs for CitySim and ENVI-met, introduces Physiological Equivalent Temperature in CitySim, and quantifies urban heat mitigation scenarios on two Swiss case studies.

projects.title: Automatic identification of flight information from speech
projects.summary: Aims to develop a unified model, for example adapting BERT, that maps speech directly to aviation call-signs, and compare it with independently trained speech recognition and concept-extraction modules.

projects.title: Understanding generalization in deep learning
projects.summary: Studies how the inductive biases of architectures and data properties explain generalization in deep learning, through experiments with various architectures and datasets, with theoretical or practical emphasis depending on the student.

projects.title: Using large pretrained language models in speech recognition
projects.summary: Measures how large pretrained language models perform in ASR by scoring the outputs of a speech recognition model and combining the scores to refine transcriptions, comparing model sizes and families and the value of retraining the language model.

projects.title: Structure-Aware Generative Models for Spatiotemporal Systems
projects.summary: The student will explore how to incorporate structural information into generative models such as diffusion and flow matching models to learn the dynamics of sensor networks in industrial systems. The goal is to improve the effectiveness and efficiency of these models for spatiotemporal signal processing.

projects.title: Physics-Informed Graph Neural Networks for Composite Material Simulation
projects.summary: The student will add physics and engineering inductive bias to a state-of-the-art graph neural network surrogate for finite element simulations, to improve performance and stability. The goal is to evaluate stable rollouts and simulate dynamic oscillations of simple structures such as composite plates.

projects.title: Accurate Simulation of Materials with Graph Neural Network Finite Element Models
projects.summary: The student will incorporate material constitutive laws into a graph neural network so that it predicts material stress accurately, instead of relying only on the parameters tracked in the dataset. The project evaluates this physics-informed approach against learning stress as a distinct objective.

projects.title: Federated Foundation Models for Electricity Load Forecasting
projects.summary: The project explores federated adaptation of time-series foundation models, using parameter-efficient methods such as LoRA, for electricity load forecasting on smart-meter data. The student will build a federated fine-tuning pipeline and benchmark it against zero-shot, local fine-tuning and centralised training.

projects.title: Data-Driven Prioritization of Railway Track Inspections
projects.summary: This semester project uses historical SBB track measurements, infrastructure data and maintenance records to test whether data-driven methods can identify track sections likely to need maintenance. The goal is to design predictive models and prioritization strategies for railway inspection within a limited inspection budget.

projects.title: Building Self-Improving AI Research Agents for Prognostics and Health Management
projects.summary: The project aims to develop a self-improving agentic AI system that extracts structured knowledge from prognostics and health management research papers and links it to benchmark tasks and evaluation criteria. The expected outcome is a prototype literature-to-evaluation pipeline for PHM research agents.

projects.title: Battery Lifetime Prediction under Changing Operating Conditions with Neural SDEs
projects.summary: This semester project develops Neural Stochastic Differential Equations to model battery degradation and predict capacity and remaining useful life under changing future operating conditions. The student will use NASA's ProgPy battery simulator and evaluate on unseen operating schedules.

projects.title: Robust Multi-Modal 3D Reconstruction
projects.summary: The project aims to make 3D scene reconstruction (NeRF and Gaussian Splatting) robust to missing pixel-level alignment between RGB and other modalities, with a focus on RGB and thermal imaging. The student will investigate contrastive learning for cross-modal correspondences and 3D feature alignment.

projects.title: Test-time Domain Adaptation for OOD Detection
projects.summary: The student will work on out-of-distribution detection under domain shift by applying test-time domain adaptation online during inference. The goal is to explore existing test-time adaptation methods and improve and modify them for OOD detection.

projects.title: Exploring Mimed and Covert Speech Decoding from EEG
projects.summary: Design and validate an EEG experiment for mimed and covert speech, collect a dataset, and assess the feasibility of decoding a small vocabulary. The project also studies which electrode locations and reduced channel configurations are most informative for speech decoding. It is designed for two students, each responsible for one speech condition.

projects.title: Patient-Independent Seizure Detection from Intracranial EEG
projects.summary: Develop deep learning methods for seizure detection from intracranial EEG that generalize across patients. Students will evaluate models on public datasets and study how learned neural representations improve robustness and cross-subject generalization.

projects.title: Speech Decoding for Brain-Computer Interfaces
projects.summary: Develop and evaluate deep learning models that decode speech from neural activity for speech BCIs. The project explores strategies to improve generalization across sessions or conditions and analyzes learned neural representations.

projects.title: Circuit Design and Verification for a Low-Power Neural Network Accelerator for Neural Decoding
projects.summary: Design and verify low-power, near-threshold circuits, including a level shifter and SRAM, for a neural network accelerator used in neuromodulation systems. Students will review literature, define specifications with PhD researchers, and evaluate a fabricated integrated circuit.

projects.title: Accurate movement trajectory decoding for high-performance brain-machine interfaces
projects.summary: Build a regressor that decodes continuous movement trajectories (hand and finger positions) from ECoG and/or spiking activity in patients. Students will study neural biomarkers and implement feature-engineered and end-to-end machine learning models.

projects.title: Circuit design for stimulation artifact cancellation in concurrent neural recording and stimulation
projects.summary: Design artifact cancellation circuits in Cadence to remove large stimulation artifacts from low-amplitude neural recordings during concurrent recording and stimulation. Students will explore algorithms and hardware architectures, assess complexity, and help design and test prototype integrated circuits.

projects.title: Resource-efficient machine learning algorithm design for on-implant neurological symptom detection
projects.summary: Develop efficient machine learning models that process electrophysiological data (scalp EEG, ECoG, spikes) in real time with low power, small on-chip area and fast inference for neurological symptom detection on implants. Students will implement models, evaluate them, and estimate hardware complexity.

projects.title: Machine learning chip design for on-implant neural decoding
projects.summary: Design an efficient feature extraction and/or machine learning processor that classifies or decodes neural data in real time on implants, with low power and small area. Students will design candidate algorithms in Cadence and assess hardware complexity with simulations, then help test prototype integrated circuits.

projects.title: Detecting mental fatigue and symptoms of psychiatric disorders from continuous neuronal recordings
projects.summary: Explore machine learning tools to detect the onset of mental fatigue and neuropsychiatric symptoms from multi-channel ECoG and LFP recordings in primates (and possibly humans). Students will study biomarkers and optimize classifiers for accuracy and latency.

projects.title: Exploring Representation Learning for Neural Signal Decoders
projects.summary: Improve representation learning for neural signal decoders, such as vector-quantization on transformer-based neural foundation models or self-supervised methods, to decode ECoG signals from movement attempts for a Brain Spine Interface. Detailed objectives are flexible and can be discussed.

projects.title: Energy-Efficient and Interpretable Neuromorphic Decoding for Neural Signal and Movement Decoding
projects.summary: The project aims to co-design energy-efficient, reliable and interpretable neuromorphic architectures for decoding neural or muscle signals (EMG, ECoG, LFP, intracortical spikes, IMU data) using spiking neural networks. It also quantifies the trade-offs in accuracy, latency, model size and energy between these neuromorphic decoders and state-of-the-art deep learning decoders for implantable brain-computer interfaces.

projects.title: Dataset Acquisition for Low-Light Image Denoising
projects.summary: Capture a new dataset of noisy/clean image pairs and dark calibration frames at many exposure times to extend the 2-Shots in the Dark low-light denoising method. The student would sort and preprocess the data and publish it on Hugging Face with a dataset card.

projects.title: Open-Source Work on Dynamic High-level Synthesis Compiler Targeting FPGAs
projects.summary: Contribute to Dynamatic, an open-source dynamic high-level synthesis compiler built on MLIR that generates RTL for FPGAs from C/C++. Work can cover compiler passes at different lowering levels, or debugging, visualisation and benchmarking tools; contributions are intended to become part of the codebase.

projects.title: Accelerate FPGA Implementation Time
projects.summary: Reduce the FPGA bitstream implementation time generated from high-level synthesis code, from several minutes to a few seconds.

projects.title: Postquantum Cryptography Core Using High-Level Synthesis
projects.summary: Explore and improve the quality of results of post-quantum cryptography hardware cores produced with high-level synthesis, compared with RTL-based designs.

projects.title: Low-Level Optimization of Dynamically Scheduled Circuits
projects.summary: Optimise dynamically scheduled circuits after the DHLS compiler output, working on RTL-to-physical FPGA implementation in Vivado during logic synthesis and place-and-route to account for real routing delays and congestion.

projects.title: Toward Coarse-Grained Field Programmable Gate Arrays
projects.summary: Study a coarser-grained, word-level version of FPGAs and evaluate its performance as a reconfigurable computing fabric, including compiler optimisations, architectural ideas, and physical implementation and modelling.

projects.title: Optimizing place and route for high frequency task parallel FPGA accelerators
projects.summary: Increase the clock frequency of HardCilk-generated FPGA circuits by adding elastic buffers to their ready-valid interfaces, and analyse the results using Vivado place and route.

projects.title: SOC-graphical configurator as VS-code plug-in
projects.summary: Develop a VS Code plug-in that provides a graphical tool for composing OpenRisc-based SoC designs for the CS-473 and CS-476 courses, generating top-level Verilog and memory maps, and exporting designs as TikZ pictures and PDF.

projects.title: Hardware coherence on various wishbone bus-architectures
projects.summary: Design and implement software-configurable hardware cache coherence protocols (such as MSI and MESI) on wishbone shared, crossbar and ring bus architectures, for a system based on Hazard3 RISC-V CPUs.

projects.title: The World as a Canvas: Multimodal Realignment of Historical Map Archives
projects.summary: Develop a multimodal method to georeference historical maps at scale by combining textual cues and latent image representations from a domain-specific vision foundation model, matching map features to contemporary geodata via keypoints and graph neural networks.

projects.title: The Origins of Venice
projects.summary: Create a digital urban atlas of Venice for 1100 and 1350 from OCR-processed historiographical sources, and use it to analyse land ownership and land uses. The goal includes an interactive Leaflet cartography and statistical analysis of ownership, land use and family names.

projects.title: The space of Victorian London
projects.summary: Study how 19th and 20th century urban interventions affected the social-spatial structure of London, by enriching an 1890s Ordnance Survey building and text dataset with infrastructure and economic data and linking it to social class data from Booth's map.

projects.title: Beyond Cheese and Chocolate: The Economic Landscape of Historical Switzerland
projects.summary: Realign the addresses of Swiss commercial registers (1883 onward) into geographic coordinates using modern geospatial references and historical place-name databases, to reconstruct the historical economic landscape of Switzerland and analyse it spatially.

projects.title: Enlumina
projects.summary: Index the visual elements of illuminated medieval manuscripts by segmenting and annotating depictions, training supervised and unsupervised (multimodal LLM) methods, and building a prototype search engine searchable by text and by visual similarity. The project also aims to study authorship attribution of copyists through visual similarity.

projects.title: Door-to-door
projects.summary: Analyse a 10-year sample of 1880 Lausanne city directories extracted via OCR, then compare trades with Paris and New York datasets, to understand the specific commercial signature of each city. Datasets are to be published online.

projects.title: The Hidden Grammar of Art History
projects.summary: Work with OCR extracted from about 300,000 digitised art-historical cardboards (Replica project) to realign artist name entities and derive heuristics about the grammar of artist attribution. An associated paper is planned.

projects.title: Lausanne 1722
projects.summary: Enrich the already georeferenced and vectorised Melotte cadastre of Lausanne (1721-1722) with socio-economic information on land use, function and ownership, to create historical geodata for studying the city's 18th-century landscape.

projects.title: European Postcards
projects.summary: Geolocate and reposition historical postcards of European places from Europeana using an AI-based semantic identifier and prompting, then publish them in the Time Machine Atlas interface. The project also involves working with the APIs of OpenAI and other AI providers.

projects.title: Cartonomics / Visual semiotics
projects.summary: Extract and analyse the visual symbols and representational elements of cartography across a large map corpus, studying how conventions for relief, elevation, buildings, water and natural landscape evolved over time, using deep learning and statistical methods.

projects.title: The Cultural Microscope
projects.summary: Design and build a prototype interface to explore 'memes' (replicated visual elements) across tens of thousands of digitised historical maps, using digital embeddings and IIIF images, and allowing switching between visual elements and their source maps.

projects.title: Automatic georeferencing of historical cadastres
projects.summary: Develop automatic computer vision and graph neural network methods to georeference the sheets of the Napoleonic and renovated European cadastres, enabling large-scale studies of territorial change over two centuries.

projects.title: Automatic transcription of Polier notebooks
projects.summary: Automatically transcribe the handwritten Polier notebooks (1754-1791, about 26,300 pages) using handwritten text recognition, then apply NLP-based distant reading to research economic, social or environmental history in Lausanne.

projects.title: Haussmannian transformations in Paris during the XIXth century
projects.summary: Convert the 19th-century Paris maps of the Bibliothèque historique de la Ville de Paris from raster into vector geometry using CNN-based pixelwise classification and classic computer vision, then quantitatively analyse the transformation of the urban fabric.

projects.title: Automatic vectorization of the renovated cadastre of Lausanne
projects.summary: Transform the 1888 renovated cadastre of Lausanne (over 300 plates) into vector maps using CNN-based semantic segmentation, and optionally use handwritten text recognition to process its legend of land uses and owners.

projects.title: Icono Lausanne – Reorientation of the photographic archives of the Historical Museum
projects.summary: Develop automatic photogrammetry and neural network methods to match the roughly 38,500 digitised photographs of the Historical Museum of Lausanne and infer their camera angle and position, enabling reprojection of historical photographs onto 4D models.

projects.title: 3D density map embedding for cryoEM
projects.summary: Build density map embeddings that capture the information in the cryoEM voxel grid using an autoencoder, and evaluate their biological meaningfulness. The project is a collaboration between the Laboratory for Biomolecular Modeling and the Computer Vision Laboratory.

projects.title: When is a good predictor a good model?
projects.summary: Investigates which model-brain comparison metrics, stimuli and experiments can distinguish artificial neural networks that truly share the brain's mechanisms from those that only predict neural activity well. The student will record from networks that solve the same task with the same or different mechanisms, apply metrics such as linear predictivity, RSA and CKA, and test whether lesions predict effects on the target system.

projects.title: Training spiking networks to generate fast time-varying patterns
projects.summary: Investigates whether spiking networks of SRM0 neurons with escape noise can be trained, using FORCE-type online learning and exact population rate equations, to produce fast and complex time-varying patterns. The project also explores which kinds of patterns can be learned when there are no constraints on the speed of the dynamics.
skills: strong background in mathematics, physics or computer science

projects.title: A Digital Twin for collective decision making
projects.summary: Build on an existing pipeline that fits Digital Twins to zebrafish behaviour recorded in response to virtual conspecifics. The project starts with an auto-regressive generative model as a baseline, then uses interpretable approaches to understand fish decision making, ideally producing predictions testable in real animals.

projects.title: Implementing and extending a biologically inspired computational model of spatial navigation in rodents
projects.summary: Implement in code a rodent navigation model with a taxon pathway (visual input to motor actions via dorsal striatum-like mechanisms) and a locale pathway (grid and place cells feeding the ventral striatum). Validate the model in reorientation and watermaze paradigms, then extend it in several possible directions.

projects.title: Modeling perceptual rules of social interactions in single animal virtual reality
projects.summary: Use computational modelling and machine learning on existing zebrafish behaviour recordings from dots projected on a screen to test whether visual preference for a virtual conspecific arises from hard-wired motion tuning or from coupling to the fish's own swim cycle. If time permits, the models will be extended to predict neural signals in the fish brain.

projects.title: The use of images in health textbooks: how images and scientific discourse on gender interact between 1870 and 1940
projects.summary: Extract and classify the illustrations in about eighty French-language health manuals (1870-1940) from digitized library collections, then analyse how depictions of men and women shape medical discourse on gender. The project is part of the SNSF-funded MEDIF project and is carried out with the Institut des humanités en médecine (IHM).

projects.title: The ecology of eucalyptus: Tracing the acclimatization and exploitation of eucalyptus in Europe through 19th-century French publications
projects.summary: Use text mining on about 3,660 19th-century French books mentioning eucalyptus, harvested from Gallica, to study how publications on the tree evolved and which properties (medicinal, forestry, agricultural) were associated with it. Possible methods include co-occurrence networks, topic modelling, sentiment analysis and named entity recognition.

projects.title: The Global Footprint of the Swiss Economy and Society: A Data-Driven Analysis of Trading Patterns in the 20th Century
projects.summary: Build a pipeline to extract data from scanned Swiss trade statistics (1890-2000) and integrate it into a database, in order to support a long-term analysis of Switzerland's material and environmental footprint. The student may then examine a research question such as the evolution of the carbon footprint or of critical materials.

projects.title: Mapping Open Science Platform
projects.summary: Crawl the web to identify links between open science platforms (repositories, journals, directories, search engines), characterise the nature of these links, and generate an interactive map of the open science network.

projects.title: The 'ecosystem' of open science: Tracing the Evolution of Ecological Metaphors in Discourses on the Digital Transition of Research
projects.summary: Assemble a heterogeneous corpus of scientific, policy and oral texts on the digital transition of research, then trace the emergence and circulation of ecological metaphors either with NLP-based automated literature review or with a multi-layered diachronic network analysis.

projects.title: How Was the Climate of the French Colonies Taught? A Study of Geography Textbooks from the Late 19th Century to the Mid-20th Century
projects.summary: Use text mining on dozens of French geography textbooks from Gallica to study how the climate and meteorology of the French colonies were taught in schools between the late Second Empire and the Third Republic, and whether a hierarchy among colonial climates existed in these representations.

projects.title: Risk-Aware Selective Mixture-of-Experts for Efficient Language Modeling
projects.summary: Master thesis project proposed by the Learning and Dynamical Systems Group (Dr. Michael Muehlebach) at the Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems, in collaboration with LIONS. The page gives only the title and a link for details, so the topic is a risk-aware selective mixture-of-experts for efficient language modeling.

projects.title: Rethinking Diffusion Modeling from the Ground Up: Building a Diffusion-LLM
projects.summary: Project rethinking diffusion modeling from first principles to build a diffusion-based LLM as part of the Swiss AI Initiative. Students explore new discrete/structured diffusion formulations, prototype diffusion-LLM architectures, and compare them with autoregressive transformers, with a theoretical direction (combinatorial optimization and submodularity) and a large-scale implementation direction.

projects.title: Emerging Optimizers for Large-Batch Training (SCION, MuON, Spectral Methods)
projects.summary: MS project investigating geometry-aware optimizers such as SCION, MuON, Stochastic Spectral Descent and Frank-Wolfe-based variants for stable large-batch training of deep networks. Students characterize their memory footprint, preconditioning, critical batch size and stability versus Adam/Lion/Shampoo, and evaluate them on large-batch pipelines (transformers, MoE).

projects.title: Online Adaptation and Dynamic Geometry in Modern Optimizers
projects.summary: MS project on online adaptation mechanisms for geometry-aware optimizers, such as dynamically adjusting preconditioners, spectral norms, constraint radii, learning rates and FW-LMO approximations during training. The goal is to design low-memory algorithms that adapt to curvature and distribution drift, tested on large-scale training setups.

projects.title: Applications of Spectral/Conditional-Gradient Optimizers in FL, RL, and Reasoning
projects.summary: MS project exploring where spectral and conditional-gradient optimizers (SCION/MuON-style) bring benefits beyond supervised training, namely federated learning, reinforcement learning and LLM-based reasoning. Students benchmark these optimizers against conventional baselines in those settings.

projects.title: Low-power analog-to-digital conversion for multichannel neural recording
projects.summary: Design and evaluation of SAR and VCO-based analog-to-digital converters for low-power multichannel neural signal recording. The student(s) model both architectures, then do transistor-level design and post-layout performance evaluation.

projects.title: Hardware-friendly selective feature extractors for neural classification tasks
projects.summary: Develop dimensionality reduction in hardware-friendly feature extractors for neural signal classification, so that data transfer is reduced and the extractors can be ported to implantable hardware. The main task is to make the DNN classifier select features near the optimal complexity/performance trade-off.

projects.title: Ultra-wideband (UWB) wireless data transfer for neural recording implants
projects.summary: Demonstrate the feasibility of a learning-based neural data compression algorithm in terms of communication power efficiency over an ultra-wideband wireless link. The main task is to control and test transmitter and receiver boards based on the Decawave IC.
skills: FPGA or MCU programming (Raspberry Pi, Arduino, MSP, PIC, etc.)

projects.title: Neural network-based hardware decoder design
projects.summary: Design of digital hardware implementing neural-network-based decoders for wireless implantable brain-activity monitoring systems aimed at spinal cord injury locomotion restoration. The student surveys recent approaches, then performs the semi-custom digital hardware design of the decoder.

projects.title: Data Processing for a Filter based Miniature Photo-Spectrometer
projects.summary: Estimate the spectrum of an unknown light source by processing the filter matrix obtained from characterising a miniature photo-spectrometer (N optical filters on a photo-sensor array, CSEM). The data processing for this filter-based spectrometer is not yet established.

projects.title: Deep Generative Models for Conditional Sampling
projects.summary: The project aims to build on recent works on learning conditional distributions p(x_unobserved | x_observed) with deep generative models such as VAEs, GANs, normalizing flows and score-based models. Open questions include integrating prior information into generative models and understanding trade-offs between generative approaches.

projects.title: Sampling, Reconstruction and Uncertainty Quantification for MRI
projects.summary: Study how deep learning methods can jointly or alternatively optimise MRI sampling (which data to acquire) and reconstruction, using reconstruction uncertainty as a quantity to minimise. The student may explore research directions such as non-Cartesian MRI or reinforcement learning approaches.

projects.title: Optimal Pick and Place Strategy for an Isochronic Robot
projects.summary: Find optimal pick-and-place sequences for Isochronic's multi-rail robot, which transports several parts simultaneously, in order to reduce total transport time. The project uses reinforcement learning, with a kinematic robot model and customer applications provided by Isochronic, and aims for a learning framework that generalises to new applications.

projects.title: Risk-Aware Selective Mixture-of-Experts for Efficient Language Modeling
projects.summary: The project extends the risk-aware selective language modeling framework (ESLM) to Mixture-of-Experts architectures by designing a risk-aware routing mechanism that routes inputs to experts based on confidence and risk estimates. The goal is more efficient training and inference with robustness to distribution shifts and adversarial inputs, evaluated against standard MoE routing strategies.

projects.title: Accelerating Geophysical Flow Simulation Using Machine Learning
projects.summary: Develop surrogate models based on machine learning, including data-driven and physics-informed approaches, to approximate physics-based geophysical flow simulations (landslides, rockfalls, snow avalanches) on complex 3D terrain at much lower computational cost. The project is supervised jointly with the Chair of Alpine Mass Movements at ETHZ.

projects.title: Digital Twin Simulation of Rockfall Hazards
projects.summary: Build a digital twin of real Alpine slopes and protection barriers from terrain reconstruction and rock geometry characterization, simulate rockfall trajectories with the in-house Discrete Element Method (DEM) code, and use uncertainty quantification and machine learning surrogates for risk mapping.

projects.title: AI-Enhanced Characterization of Internal Material Properties from Surface Observations
projects.summary: Develop a generalized AI-based inverse modeling framework, using deep learning, that infers internal material property distributions from observable surface responses, for applications such as structural diagnostics and non-destructive evaluation.

projects.title: Experimental Investigation of Architected Granular Materials
projects.summary: Design and 3D-print custom particle geometries, assemble granular packings with controlled structure, and run static and dynamic mechanical tests with imaging and digital image correlation to link particle-scale properties to macroscale response of programmable granular materials.

projects.title: Segregation in Granular Flows
projects.summary: Use numerical simulations to study how particle shape and size influence segregation under shear and gravity-driven granular flows, by analyzing inter-particle forces, to support continuum modeling of segregation.

projects.title: Graph Neural Networks for Granular Mechanics
projects.summary: Apply Graph Neural Networks to grain-scale force chain networks in granular materials approaching unjamming and failure, training on discrete element simulations and grain-resolved experimental data to connect grain-scale patterns with macroscopic behavior.

projects.title: Physics-informed Neural Operators for Solid Mechanics
projects.summary: Explore physics-informed neural operators (PINOs) to simulate material behavior under various loading conditions in geotechnical or structural engineering problems, and compare their accuracy and generalization with conventional numerical solutions.

projects.title: Frictional Instabilities in Topologically Interlocked Structures
projects.summary: Investigate how stick-slip frictional instabilities and interfacial heterogeneity drive sudden failures and load drops in topologically interlocked structures, using the level-set discrete element modeling framework.

projects.title: Phase-field Modeling of Fracture of Architected Structural Materials
projects.summary: Develop and apply phase-field fracture models to simulate crack initiation and propagation in architected materials such as truss lattices and bioinspired composites, and explore machine-learning surrogates for phase-field evolution to reduce computational cost.

projects.title: Multiphysics Modeling of Fault Gouge
projects.summary: Combine discrete and continuum simulations to study fault gouge rheology, including the effects of material heterogeneity, grain-scale characteristics, particle fracture, and hydromechanical and thermomechanical coupling, to understand earthquake mechanics.

projects.title: Frictional instabilities in topologically interlocked structures
projects.summary: The project studies how stick-slip frictional instabilities and interfacial heterogeneity affect the failure of topologically interlocked structures. The student will use the level-set discrete element modeling framework to investigate their dynamic behavior under various conditions.

projects.title: Graph Neural Networks for Granular Mechanics
projects.summary: The project uses Graph Neural Networks to study how force-chain networks in granular materials evolve under shear, focusing on the approach to unjamming and failure. Models are to be trained on discrete element simulations and grain-scale experimental measurements.

projects.title: Multiphysics modeling of fault gouge
projects.summary: The student will combine discrete and continuum simulations to study fault gouge rheology, focusing on material heterogeneity, grain-scale characteristics such as particle fracture, and hydromechanical and thermomechanical coupling. The goal is to gain insight into earthquake mechanics.

projects.title: Physics-informed Deep Neural Operators for Solid Mechanics
projects.summary: The student explores the application of physics-informed deep neural operators (PINOs) to solid mechanics problems, simulating material behavior under various loading conditions in geotechnical or structural engineering contexts. The generalization ability of the method is evaluated and its accuracy is compared with conventional numerical solutions.

projects.title: Segregation in Granular Flows
projects.summary: Numerical study of how particle shape and size affect segregation of particles under shear and gravity-driven granular flow, by analysing the inter-particle forces. The goal is to inform continuum modelling of segregation in different scenarios.

projects.title: Accelerating geophysical flow simulation using machine learning
projects.summary: Develop machine learning surrogate models, purely data-driven or physics-informed, that approximate high-fidelity physics-based geophysical flow simulations (e.g., MPM or DEM on 3D terrains) at a much lower computational cost. The surrogate is to be evaluated on velocity fields, runout distances and deposition patterns on unseen terrains. The project is supervised jointly with the Chair of Alpine Mass Movements at ETH Zurich.

projects.title: AI-Enhanced Characterization of Internal Material Properties from Surface Observations
projects.summary: Develop a generalized inverse modeling framework that uses deep learning to infer internal material property distributions from observable surface responses such as displacement fields. The approach uses high-fidelity simulations, robust feature extraction and regularization to handle the ill-posedness of the inverse problem.

projects.title: Digital twin simulation of rockfall hazards
projects.summary: Develop a digital twin framework for simulating and assessing rockfall hazards in real-world terrains, using terrain reconstruction and the lab's in-house DEM code to model rockfall trajectories and barrier interactions. The project also explores uncertainty quantification and machine learning surrogate models for risk mapping.

projects.title: Experimental Investigation of Architected Granular Materials
projects.summary: The project studies architected granular materials, where particle shape, surface properties and packing are designed to control macroscopic mechanical behavior. Students will 3D-print custom particles, assemble granular packings, run static and dynamic mechanical tests with digital image correlation and imaging, and link microscale interactions to macroscale stiffness and energy absorption.

projects.title: Phase-field modeling of fracture in architected structural materials
projects.summary: The project aims to develop and apply phase-field fracture models to simulate crack initiation and propagation in architected materials such as truss lattices and bioinspired composites. The goal is to understand how microstructural features (periodicity, hierarchy, intentional defects) affect fracture toughness, fracture modes and energy dissipation, with an option to explore machine-learning surrogate models for phase-field evolution.

projects.title: Accelerating Geophysical Flow Simulation Using Machine Learning
projects.summary: Develop and train a fast machine-learning emulator for geophysical flows such as landslides, rockfalls and snow avalanches, using material point simulation data and remote sensing data. The goal is to replace costly physics-based simulations.

projects.title: Digital Twin Simulation of Rockfall Hazards
projects.summary: Build a computational framework based on the Discrete Element Method to predict rockfall runout, accounting for boulder shape derived from drone imagery and for boulder fragmentation.

projects.title: Discovering Internal Material Properties from Surface Observations
projects.summary: Use physics-informed neural operators to infer internal material properties from data available on the boundary of a body. Applications mentioned include subsurface engineering and material testing.

projects.title: Segregation in granular flows
projects.summary: Study segregation mechanisms in granular flows and how particle shape affects this process, using the Discrete Element Method.

projects.title: Multiphysics Modeling of Fault Gouge
projects.summary: Study the contact mechanics and multiphysics (thermal and fluid) processes of fault gouge, from both discrete and continuum modeling perspectives, to better understand earthquakes.

projects.title: Experimental Investigation of Architected Granular Materials
projects.summary: Experimentally explore architected granular materials (granular crystals and quasicrystals) for penetration applications.

projects.title: Phase-field Modeling of Fracture of Architected Structural Materials
projects.summary: Develop a micromechanics-informed phase-field computational model, potentially combined with deep learning, to capture fracture in architected materials and compare it against ongoing experiments.

projects.title: Concept-based representations in pretrained vision models: concept bottleneck models vs sparse autoencoders
projects.summary: Compares concept bottleneck models (CBMs), sparse autoencoders (SAEs), and hybrids of the two for learning concept-oriented representations in pretrained vision models. The goal is to assess interpretability, disentanglement, information leakage, and downstream usefulness.

projects.title: Learning from Art Brut: reading cognitive signatures in artworks
projects.summary: Applies deep learning and computer vision to digitised Art Brut collections from Lausanne, Bern and Heidelberg to extract and cluster recurrent visual patterns across diagnoses and artists. The aim is to find cognitive signatures of mental disorders, in collaboration with art-history and symbolism experts.

projects.title: Machine learning for molecular identification from tandem mass spectra
projects.summary: Aims to identify small molecules from tandem mass spectrometry data, which mostly remain unmatched to structures. Possible directions include conditional graph generative models, self-supervised foundation models for spectra, combinatorial optimization over molecular space, and uncertainty quantification. The project has a strong research focus and may lead to a publication.

projects.title: Mechanistic interpretability of looped diffusion language models
projects.summary: Studies and compares the internal dynamics of standard masked diffusion language models and looped/recursive variants using lens-based interpretability tools such as Logit Lens, Tuned Lens and Jacobian Lens. The goal is to understand how and when predictions form across layers, loops and denoising steps.

projects.title: Graph diffusion with joint node-edge constraints
projects.summary: Aims to develop a graph diffusion method that natively enforces joint node-edge constraints during generation, such as valence consistency in molecular graphs. The goal is to improve state-of-the-art performance on real-world tasks such as molecular design.

projects.title: Low-rank edge representations for scalable graph transformers
projects.summary: Investigates low-rank edge representations in graph transformers used for graph diffusion, to reduce the memory cost of the dense edge state. The project quantifies expressivity of low-rank edges and tests an implementation on benchmarks, including large graphs.

projects.title: Optimal-transport-based train/test splits for distribution shift
projects.summary: Develops optimization-based methods that build challenging train/test splits by maximizing the optimal transport discrepancy between training and test sets. The project has five difficulty levels, scaled to bachelor, master short-project, or master thesis scope, and requires efficient algorithms for large datasets.

projects.title: Neural ODE graph networks for latent graph trajectories
projects.summary: Uses a Neural ODE formulation to learn latent graph trajectories with graph neural networks for temporal data, separating spatial and temporal updates. The goal is interpretability of the flow field and learning in scarce-data settings.

projects.title: Topoformer: A Spatial-Informed Foundation Model for Spatial-Biology
projects.summary: Builds a foundation model for spatial biology by converting tissue images into compact spatial tokens using topological data analysis, then training transformers with self-supervised pretraining on large public cohorts. Target tasks include patient stratification, survival prediction and biomarker discovery.

projects.title: Robust Automatic Pathological Speech Detection
projects.summary: Develops robust deep learning approaches for automatic pathological speech detection that withstand recording artifacts and spurious correlations such as noise disparity between classes. The aim is to support clinical assessment of speech disorders.

projects.title: Physics-Informed Graph Neural Networks for High-Resolution Mesh-Based Simulations
projects.summary: Explores physics-informed graph neural networks to scale mesh-based simulations to high resolution, using coarser surrogate representations and hierarchical multi-scale modeling. The initial testbed is wind-tunnel dynamics.

projects.title: Graph Latent Diffusion Models
projects.summary: Aims to develop a graph-specific latent diffusion model that runs the diffusion process in a lower-dimensional latent space, to scale graph generation beyond small graphs.

projects.title: Scalable Graph Generation via Link Prediction
projects.summary: Aims to make graph generation scalable by replacing quadratic-cost sparse graph transformers with message-passing and link prediction modules that match transformer performance. Goals include reproducing SparseDiff and exploring other scalable methods such as latent diffusion.

projects.title: Synthetic Stroke Lesion Simulation and Deep Learning Segmentation Using HCP Data
projects.summary: Develop a simulation framework that generates synthetic acute stroke lesions on high-quality HCP diffusion and structural MRI, then train a deep segmentation network on this synthetic data. The trained model is to be evaluated on real stroke images from open clinical datasets such as ISLES and on CHUV network prototypes.

projects.title: Deep Neural Network uncertainty quantification: beyond Deep Ensemble
projects.summary: Survey whether the reconstruction quality and uncertainty estimates of a deep ensemble can be obtained at lower cost with a single network or modified architecture. Compare input perturbation, weight perturbation (e.g. Laplace-style approximation), and Bayesian neural network architectures.

projects.title: Physics-Informed Learning for Sparse Measurement Selection in Diffusion MRI Protocol Design
projects.summary: Use machine learning to select a compact subset of diffusion MRI measurements that remains informative for estimating white matter model parameters, guided by physics-informed criteria such as Fisher information. The learned protocol is to be compared with baseline selection strategies using simulations and parameter estimation.

projects.title: Development of a pre-processing pipeline for diffusion-weighted MRI data followed by the implementation of a deep-learning-based automatic lymph-node segmentation tool
projects.summary: Build a body DW-MRI pre-processing pipeline with quality control and non-rigid co-registration, then design and evaluate a deep-learning model that automatically segments lymph nodes from the co-registered volumes. The work also compares supervised, transfer-learning and self/unsupervised data strategies.

projects.title: Wavefield Extrapolation in Polar Coordinates for Ultrasound Imaging in Heterogeneous Media
projects.summary: Derive and implement a paraxial approximation of the 2D Helmholtz equation in polar coordinates to extrapolate acoustic wavefields over smoothly varying sound-speed media for curved ultrasound arrays. The solver is to be validated on simulated ultrasound data and benchmarked for accuracy, stability and efficiency, and released as open-source code.

projects.title: Data-driven wave propagation modeling for ultrasound imaging
projects.summary: Investigate data-driven modeling strategies that build a proxy for the wave propagation operator directly from recorded ultrasound signals, avoiding full-wave simulations. The goal is a low-dimensional, cheap model compared against model-based wavefields across media of varying complexity.

projects.title: Project at CHUV – Mapping functional connectivity in callosal dysgenesis
projects.summary: Analyse ADC-fMRI data from a cohort of children with callosal dysgenesis, from diffusion MRI timeseries preprocessing to group comparisons of brain activity and functional connectivity. The project is based at the CHUV Radiology Research Unit with a start date of Fall 2026.

projects.title: Contrastive latent alignment for multimodal reasoning
projects.summary: Explore a contrastive latent alignment process that enforces cross-modal and preference alignment within continuous latent reasoning paths, to handle conflicting sensory inputs that corrupt latent representations. Suggested methods include cross-modal contrastive trajectory optimization and direct preference alignment over continuous latent manifolds.

projects.title: Locating and ablating circuit-level private attribute sub-networks
projects.summary: Use activation-space dictionary learning to map the circuits that encode specific private attributes (PII) in AI models, then ablate or orthogonalize these latent directions. The goal is to remove PII while preserving zero-shot task performance, without retraining or fine-tuning the model.

projects.title: Continuous latent flow matching for multimodal spatial reasoning
projects.summary: Develop a single-step continuous latent flow architecture that maps directly from multimodal inputs (video, audio, language instructions) to latent action-reasoning representations for Vision-Language-Action models. The aim is accurate spatial problem-solving in a single forward pass, replacing multi-step chain-of-thought generation.

projects.title: Alignment-based conformance checking
projects.summary: Build a neuro-symbolic conformance checking framework that translates natural language regulatory articles (e.g. EU AI Act, GDPR) into linear temporal logic specifications and evaluates them on execution traces of multi-agent systems. The aim is a transparent mechanism that detects and explains compliance risks.

projects.title: Visual stream parsing for compliance auditing
projects.summary: Design a dynamic legal-visual (or legal-audio-visual) concept engine that extends static concept probing to real-time video streams. It would fuse vision-language or audio-visual-language streaming backbones with ontology graph mapping to track entities, infer sensitive personal attributes and map scene semantics to legal frameworks.

projects.title: Voice anonymization with preservation of emotional prosody in multilingual settings
projects.summary: Design, implement and evaluate an AI-based acoustic transformation framework that masks speaker identity while preserving emotional prosody, semantic meaning and intelligibility. The focus is French/Italian or German, including Swiss German, with evaluation with human participants and real-world datasets in collaboration with RTS.

projects.title: Linguistic and stylometric style transfer for long-form speech anonymization
projects.summary: Use sequence-to-sequence style-transfer models to translate or obfuscate individual speaking styles, syntax and dialectal markers in long-form recordings, so speakers cannot be re-identified from linguistic cues. The focus is French/Italian or German, including Swiss German, with evaluation with human participants and real-world datasets in collaboration with RTS.

projects.title: Privacy guarantees for speech anonymization
projects.summary: Build a framework that explicitly bounds and minimizes mutual information across speech modalities (acoustic, emotional prosody, linguistic stylometrics), providing information-theoretic privacy guarantees against adaptive adversaries. The work combines AI signal processing, deep generative modeling and privacy theory, with evaluation with human participants and RTS data.

projects.title: Analysing the Effect of Assistant Post-Training on Diversity and Sycophancy in Pedagogical LLMs
projects.summary: Studies how diversity, sycophancy and safety change across the post-training stages (base, SFT, DPO, RLVR) of the open model Olmo 3 7B when generating feedback on open-ended student work. The project aims to find internal features linked to these behaviours and to test lightweight interventions (weight interpolation, feature steering, short LoRA fine-tuning) that improve diversity and reduce sycophancy without undermining safety.

projects.title: Robustness of LLM Reasoning Strategies for Educational Applications
projects.summary: Investigates how different reasoning strategies (linear, symbolic, reflective, iterative) affect the robustness and reliability of LLMs under controlled perturbations in educational tasks such as misconception detection and educational content generation. It evaluates accuracy, explanation consistency, error propagation, recovery and the trade-off with computational cost.

projects.title: Mapping Failures of AI Agents on Educational Tasks
projects.summary: Analyses a dataset of agent interactions across six learning contexts to map failures of agentic AI systems on education tasks (understanding the learning context and modelling learner data) to generic failure taxonomies. The goal is to develop an education-specific coding scheme, combine manual and LLM-based trace analysis, and identify where existing taxonomies need refinement.

projects.title: Do Questions Trigger Misconceptions? Measuring When Student Misconceptions Show Up
projects.summary: Uses existing anonymised Eedi diagnostic maths responses to measure the trigger strength of each question-misconception pair and test whether it predicts when a student's misconception reappears, controlling for ability and difficulty. It also compares a persona-prompted open LLM simulator (e.g. Qwen3-8B) with real students' misconception rates.

projects.title: Data curation and curriculum learning for pre-training, theory and practice
projects.summary: Semester project around LLM pre-training, covering data curation and curriculum learning, with both theoretical and practical components. Part of the MLO large language model project offer.

projects.title: Scaling to longer context windows through modifications of attention
projects.summary: Semester project on extending the context length of LLMs by modifying the attention mechanism. Part of the MLO large language model project offer around Apertus.

projects.title: Efficiency engineering for LLM pretraining and specifically MoE architectures
projects.summary: Semester project on improving the computational efficiency of LLM pre-training, with a focus on mixture-of-experts (MoE) architectures. Part of the MLO large language model project offer around Apertus.

projects.title: Tools-usage during pretraining & finetuning
projects.summary: Semester project on enabling tool usage by LLMs during pre-training and fine-tuning. Part of the MLO large language model project offer around Apertus.

projects.title: Safety and alignment during pretraining
projects.summary: Semester project on integrating safety and alignment considerations into LLM pre-training. Part of the MLO large language model project offer around Apertus.

projects.title: Novel architectures (including efficient long context or MoE related mechanisms)
projects.summary: Semester project on new LLM architectures, including efficient long-context and mixture-of-experts mechanisms. Part of the MLO large language model project offer around Apertus.

projects.title: Optimization dynamics for LLMs (e.g. Muon and AdEMAmix variants, and interactions with architecture)
projects.summary: Semester project studying optimization dynamics of LLM training, such as Muon and AdEMAmix variants and their interaction with architecture. Part of the MLO large language model project offer around Apertus.

projects.title: LLM inference on old V100 GPUs
projects.summary: Aims to run recent large open-weight MoE models efficiently on the EPFL cluster of V100 GPUs and compare with newer GPU versions, applying quantization and communication-efficient parallelism with inference frameworks such as vLLM or SGLang in multi-GPU settings.

projects.title: Communication-efficient gossip methods for replacing all-reduce in distributed LLM training
projects.summary: Implement decentralized pairwise averaging of model weights instead of all-to-all communication, and investigate how model and data parallelism settings and communication compression affect distributed LLM pre-training.

projects.title: AI safety evaluations feeding back into Apertus Posttraining
projects.summary: Work with UN agencies such as UNICC to incorporate findings from recent red-teaming studies into the posttraining recipes (safety SFT and RL) of the next generation Apertus model.

projects.title: LLM Pretraining Data Curation
projects.summary: Advance pre-training data curation beyond baselines such as FineWeb-2 HQ through new techniques for signal extraction, semantic filtering and partially synthetic augmentation or rephrasing, in English or multilingual settings. One idea is to study the impact of data quality on the curse of multilinguality and its relation to scaling laws.

projects.title: Learning to sample on the fly for SGD / curriculum learning
projects.summary: Train an auxiliary network that assigns scores to training data points and use these scores to select an improved set of training points, exploring several ways of training the auxiliary parameters.

projects.title: Improving factuality understanding for LLM training
projects.summary: Add a factuality tag or masking to each document to guide an LLM's understanding of what is factual, with the goal of enhancing factuality and reducing hallucinations; post-training techniques may also be investigated.

projects.title: Build decentralized LLMs in the browser
projects.summary: Practical project joining a larger team effort to build decentralized and federated training software in which many clients (e.g. phones or hospitals) collaboratively train models such as smaller LLMs while preserving data privacy; students would help integrate the Burn framework within DISCO.

projects.title: Image compression for DNA based storage
projects.summary: Study state-of-the-art approaches for storing information in DNA and build an end-to-end image compression simulator for DNA storage based on publicly available implementations. The student analyses the simulator's performance.

projects.title: Deep learning for deepfake detection
projects.summary: Train convolutional neural networks in a supervised way to detect deepfake images and videos, collecting existing deepfake datasets and studying ensembles of trained CNNs. The student assesses performance across several datasets.

projects.title: Mobile App for Privacy Protection on iOS or Android Platform
projects.summary: Develop a smartphone app that obfuscates personal visual information in images in a secure and recoverable way, with multi-region selection by touch and a simple key management system. The app should also support sharing protected images on social networks.

projects.title: Reverse image search for media-context verification in multimodal fact-checking
projects.summary: Build a component that searches the Web for earlier appearances of a submitted image and recovers their date, location and event, to improve detection of out-of-context misinformation in a JPEG Trust fact-checking pipeline. The work includes comparing candidate tools and evaluating on multimodal misinformation datasets.

projects.title: Representation and interpretation of a Factuality Trust Indicator in JPEG Trust
projects.summary: Define and implement a JPEG Trust compatible way to represent content-based factuality information in media assets, with tools to generate and read it. The student builds Trust Profile examples combining factuality with other trust information and evaluates how factuality affects the Trust Report.

projects.title: AI TOOLS – Understanding Learning Through Pipeline Transparency
projects.summary: Student project on AI tools for education, examining how pipeline transparency helps learners understand learning. The page gives only the title and a downloadable document, with no further description.

projects.title: AI tools – Impact of glass-boxing the Machine Learning pipeline on learning
projects.summary: Student project studying the impact of making the machine learning pipeline transparent (glass-boxing) on learning. The page gives only the title and a downloadable document, with no further description.

projects.title: Development of grading tool with GPT: Enhancing Efficiency and Consistency in Education
projects.summary: Develop an AI-driven grading tool using GPT models to automate grading of student solutions such as coding assignments and open-ended responses. The work compares GPT-based grading with existing human grading data and aims to improve GPT's grading through a corrective framework.

projects.title: Enhancing Debugging Skills in Education: From Task Design to Learning Analytics
projects.summary: The project aims to design effective debugging tasks and assess debugging skills using tools such as Karel programming environments and paper-based assessments. The student would test the tasks with the PISA network, design and run a study comparing them with interactive debugging tasks, and perform learning analytics and statistical analysis on users' action sequences.

projects.title: Unplugged AI Tools: Activities to Teach AI Concepts in School
projects.summary: Develop unplugged, computer-free activities that introduce foundational AI concepts to primary and middle school students. The work covers a literature review, activity and teacher-guide design, prototyping, and optional pilot testing in Swiss schools.

projects.title: Weatherproof data logging system for honeybee colony metabolic investigation
projects.summary: Design and build a weatherproof data logging system that interfaces with robotic frames, an array of CO2 sensors and a local weather station, to study the thermal and metabolic behaviour of honeybee colonies in observation hives. The system is to be installed in a real setting, and its data will be compared with measurements from empty and full hives.

projects.title: Robotic Sculptures for Education: Sthymuli - User experience programming and validation
projects.summary: Complete the development of the Sthymuli educational robot prototype by documenting it, redesigning its graphic interface and user experience, and building a web-based application for programming its modules. The work includes testing and evaluating the robot with the EPFL community and volunteer teachers.

projects.title: AI TOOLS | Impact of glass-boxing the Machine Learning pipeline on learning
projects.summary: Develop a custom web-based platform to run a study comparing three levels of transparency (glass box, gray box, black box) in a decision-tree machine learning task where users predict a dinosaur's diet from field notes. The project adapts an existing paper-based experiment to a digital environment to test whether exposing data preparation or model logic improves understanding of ML.

projects.title: Understanding Learning Through Pipeline Transparency: A Thinking-Aloud Study of the Decision-Tree Transparency Platform
projects.summary: Follow-up to a previous semester project that built a web platform for studying 'Pipeline Transparency' in ML education with three decision-tree conditions (Glass Box, Gray Box, Black Box). The student will run Thinking Aloud sessions with about 12 participants, then do a qualitative thematic analysis to characterize students' reasoning about data and model transparency and the mental models they form of the ML pipeline.

projects.title: Deep Learning Analysis of Human Histology Images
projects.summary: A semester project applying deep learning to analyse human histology images, as listed under the available semester projects. The page gives only the title and no further details.

projects.title: Latent space models for cyclic biomolecular processes and application to live microscopy imaging
projects.summary: A semester project developing latent space models for cyclic biomolecular processes, with application to live microscopy imaging. The page gives only the title and no further details.

projects.title: Machine learning multiomics data to identify gene regulatory networks across time, sex and tissues
projects.summary: A semester project using machine learning on multiomics data to identify gene regulatory networks across time, sex and tissues. The page gives only the title and no further details.

projects.title: Circadian clocks in disease states and cancer
projects.summary: A semester project studying circadian clocks in disease states and cancer. The page gives only the title and no further details.

projects.title: Using math to infer network behavior
projects.summary: Infer network behavior, such as traffic de-prioritization, using only external observations of a flow. The student would help reconstruct the queuing delay process seen by a flow from its own irregular observations.

projects.title: Testing a neutrality-detection tool
projects.summary: Final pre-deployment testing of a tool that localizes where ISPs throttle, block, or de-prioritize traffic. The work includes running experiments on various networks, analyzing results to evaluate accuracy and robustness, and suggesting improvements.

projects.title: A Cross-Species Meta-Analysis of Astrocyte Transcriptional Diversity in Development and Disease (Dry)
projects.summary: Computational meta-analysis integrating public mouse and human single-cell and single-nucleus RNA-seq and multiomics datasets to build a cross-species astrocyte transcriptomic atlas. The project maps developmental and disease-associated astrocyte states and links them to GWAS risk loci for neurological and psychiatric disorders.

projects.title: Linking Neuronal Function to Molecular Identity in Mouse Barrel Cortex (Dry and Wet)
projects.summary: Interdisciplinary project combining in vivo two-photon calcium imaging with spatial transcriptomics (Direct HybISS) to relate the activity of neurons to their molecular identity in adult mouse barrel cortex. The student contributes to an experimental pipeline that registers the same neurons across functional imaging and post-mortem transcriptomics.

projects.title: Ex utero metabolic perturbation of the developing mouse brain
projects.summary: Wet and dry lab project in which the student acutely perturbs lipid metabolism in ex utero cultured mouse embryos during early brain formation. Effects are assessed with MALDI imaging mass spectrometry, spatial transcriptomics and confocal microscopy, followed by computational integration of spatial datasets.

projects.title: Use computational tools to study neural circuit activity
projects.summary: Use computer vision and machine learning to extract neural activity patterns during behavior and make predictions linking behavioral and internal states. The project sits at the interface of computer science and neurobiology.

projects.title: Build artificial neural networks to control a simulated fly.
projects.summary: Develop biorealistic controllers for a physics-based neuromechanical simulation of the fruit fly Drosophila melanogaster. The project lies at the interface of robotics, computer science and neuroscience, possibly in collaboration with the BioRobotics Laboratory.

projects.title: Use robotic systems to automate biological experimentation
projects.summary: Develop automated vision-guided robotic systems that perform behavioral and/or neural experiments, to automate and democratize biological experimentation. The project sits at the interface of robotics and neurobiology, possibly in collaboration with the Microrobotics Laboratory.

projects.title: Use computational tools to study animal behavior
projects.summary: Use computational and machine learning approaches to quantify and segment fly behaviors into individual actions, and link these behavioral sequences to simultaneously acquired neuroimaging data.

projects.title: Study the full graph (connectome) of the fly nervous system
projects.summary: Improve and explore the fly connectome graph to answer specific questions about neural circuit motifs underlying complex motor behaviors. The project sits at the interface of computer science, mathematics and biology.

projects.title: Behavioral studies in the laboratory
projects.summary: Hands-on experimental work with flies to examine how neural activation or other perturbations modulate animal behavior. The student designs experiments and analyzes their own data.

projects.title: Build a robotic fly
projects.summary: Construct an insect-inspired robot and test bioinspired algorithms of limb control, in collaboration with EPFL robotics groups. Nature's solutions to autonomous behavioral control are to be leveraged in robotics.

projects.title: Does Personalization in Medical Collaborative Learning Learn Site Shortcuts?
projects.summary: Investigates whether standard personalized federated learning methods learn site-specific shortcuts (spurious correlations) on medical data, with the goal of informing a personalization method that keeps useful site-specific features while avoiding shortcuts.

projects.title: Whose bubble is it? Harvesting idle capacity in data-parallel, expert-parallel LLM serving
projects.summary: Characterizes where GPU idle capacity arises in data-parallel, expert-parallel Mixture-of-Experts LLM serving and determines when it can be harvested for parameter-efficient fine-tuning without violating service-level objectives through coupling between replicas.

projects.title: Noise or Lies? Distinguishing privacy protection from fairwashing in black-box audits
projects.summary: Studies when an external auditor, who only sees black-box query answers, can distinguish an honest privacy-preserving platform (random, public noise) from a manipulative platform that performs fairwashing to hide discrimination.

projects.title: Privacy Vulnerability Transfer in Model Merging
projects.summary: Studies how privacy vulnerabilities, including membership inference and extraction risks, propagate into merged language models built with model merging and task arithmetic, and how merging coefficients, number of merged models and task similarity affect this transfer.

projects.title: Learning trajectories in models and children
projects.summary: Treats language model training as a developmental trajectory and asks whether the order and timing of language abilities emerging in artificial systems match those of children. The work combines training densely checkpointed models from scratch (with learned tokenizers, joint text-vision-audio learning, and constrained initializations) with structural probing, in collaboration with developmental neuroscientists and psycholinguists.

projects.title: Characterizing Neuronal Activity in Brain Organoids Across Neurodevelopmental Disorder Mutants
projects.summary: Analyzes existing multielectrode array (MEA) recordings from brain organoids carrying neurodevelopmental disorder-associated mutations and healthy controls, quantifying network activity features such as firing rates, bursts and synchrony. The student then trains interpretable machine learning classifiers to distinguish mutant from wildtype organoids, with an optional extension on developmental timepoints.

projects.title: Action Space Reduction for Learning Robotic Manipulation (Semester Project)
projects.summary: Study how reducing the action space with eigengrasps (a low-dimensional hand synergy basis extracted by PCA from grasping data) affects reinforcement or imitation learning of dexterous manipulation with a fully actuated hand. Performance is compared against a baseline on task success rate and reward, with optional deployment on real hardware.

projects.title: Augmented Robot Reality: Projecting the Virtual into the Real World
projects.summary: The project aims to visualise virtual information in real time to augment a multi-robot testbed, overlaying robot decision-making data on camera video feeds and projecting virtual environments onto the ground. The work includes mapping camera and projector pixels to the robot configuration space, correcting lens and projector distortion, and building an interactive tool that integrates into the existing robot control system.

projects.title: Controlling soft robotic arm via MPC and reinforcement learning (Semester Project / Master Thesis)
projects.summary: The project aims to develop an accurate controller for soft robotic arms that achieves reliable trajectory tracking across varying spatial poses and payload conditions. It will explore model predictive control based on identified or neural network models, and reinforcement learning with domain randomization or adaptation.

projects.title: Fine-Tuning of Vision-Language-Action Models for Real World Robotic Manipulation Tasks (Semester Project / Master Thesis)
projects.summary: Build an end-to-end pipeline for real-robot manipulation: teleoperate the robot to collect demonstrations, create a clean dataset, and fine-tune an open-source Vision-Language-Action model to train imitation policies. The stated goal is to set up the system for the WBCD manipulation competition (What Bimanuals Can Do) at IROS 2026.

projects.title: Finetuning Policy via Reinforcement Learning from Human Preferences (Semester Project/ Master Thesis)
projects.summary: The project aims to fine-tune robotic manipulation policies with reinforcement learning from human preferences (RLHF), done offline from a pre-collected exploratory dataset to avoid costly or harmful online RL on the real system. The work includes simulation implementation and validation on the real-world robotic system.

projects.title: Information Design in Local Energy Markets (Semester Project)
projects.summary: The project applies the theory of signalling in games (Bayesian persuasion) to local energy markets, investigating whether the market operator can strategically communicate weather or renewable production forecasts to prosumers to achieve more efficient and fair outcomes. It involves literature review, implementation of signalling code, and experiments on real-world distribution grid and consumption data.

projects.title: Learning Robotic Manipulation with Tunable Compliance (Master Thesis)
projects.summary: Build an imitation learning framework for a 20-DoF Wuji Hand and a 7-DoF arm, commanded in position, with an admittance controller and demonstrations labelled by stiffness. A diffusion transformer policy conditioned on the stiffness label should make compliance tunable after training and in real time, evaluated on tasks such as pick and place under different stiffness values.

projects.title: Sim-to-Real Transfer for JetBot via Domain Randomization and Adaptation
projects.summary: Develop and evaluate reinforcement learning policies that transfer robustly from simulation to the real NVIDIA JetBot, using domain randomization, domain adaptation, and hybrid sim-real fine-tuning. The work covers simulation setup, policy training, adversarial feature alignment, and real-robot deployment with minimal fine-tuning.

projects.title: Controlling a Multi-drone Fleet for Traffic Monitoring
projects.summary: Coordinate a fleet of UAVs that collect traffic data at multiple locations, deciding where and when each drone collects data based on road importance and previous visits. The page text is truncated.

projects.title: Reinforcement learning to achieve efficient equilibria in repeated games with partial observability
projects.summary: Design online learning algorithms that learn efficient equilibria of a long-horizon repeated game, focusing on leader-follower games where the follower's actions are partially observable. Master's thesis project at the intersection of reinforcement learning and game theory.

projects.title: Multi-Objective Optimization for Automated Theorem Proving
